jobs.title: Revenue Operations Analyst, Partnerships
jobs.description:
We are on a mission to empower people of all ages to thrive in an increasingly connected world. By uniting Aura and Qoria, organizations driven by personal experiences with identity theft and cyberbullying, our combined company brings together global category leaders to create a safer internet for everyone across all stages of life. Today, our $340M+ ARR platform protects over 9 million families and 32,000 schools across 100+ countries. Driven by a global team of over 1,000 people, we are combining intelligent digital threat protection with student and child wellbeing tools so everyone can navigate the digital world safely and with confidence.

We are seeking a dynamic team player to join Aura in a new role which combines data analytics, revenue accounting, and business partnership. As part of our mission to drive consistent growth in our partner revenue channel, this position will play a critical role in aligning partner analytics with accurate revenue forecasting and GAAP-compliant reporting.

The Revenue Operations Analyst, Partnerships will collaborate closely with internal and external stakeholders to contribute towards the revenue process for our rapidly expanding partner channel. This role is responsible for ensuring accurate partner billing, analytics, and reporting.

Reporting to the Director of Partner Revenue Operations, the ideal candidate will bring strong data analytics expertise and a collaborative spirit to a role which offers a unique opportunity to contribute directly to Aura’s growth.

Day To Day

Transform source data into a usable format for monthly billing, revenue recognition, and forecasting purposes
Ensure enrollment numbers used in Employee Benefits/Partner business forecasts are aligned with source customer enrollment counts and actual enrollment counts used by Revenue Accounting for GAAP purposes
Own the ongoing health of the billing engine: perform regular QA on Python/SQL logic, monitor for discrepancies, and troubleshoot issues as they arise in production
Debug and fix existing billing engine code to resolve identified issues, ensuring minimal disruption to partner invoicing and downstream revenue reporting
Design and implement new invoicing logic and billing flows to support evolving contract structures, new partner types, or business requirements
Assist in ad hoc projects and system integrations as an SME for the Partner Revenue Operations team

What You Bring To The Table

2-3 years of progressive experience in data analytics
Proficiency in SQL and Python - ability to query and manipulate large datasets efficiently
Experience with Databricks - familiarity with data engineering and analytics in a cloud environment
Experience building data logic/pipelines — this role includes designing new invoicing flows
Translating business/contract requirements into technical logic, working iteratively with stakeholders to validate assumptions
Advanced Excel skills - including pivot tables, advanced formulas, and data analysis
Strong analytical thinking - ability to identify trends, discrepancies, and insights in financial data
Solid financial background - knowledge of financial statements, basic accounting principles, and tax implications
Attention to detail and problem-solving skills - ability to ensure data accuracy and resolve inconsistencies.
BA/BS in Analytics, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Computer Science, Economics, or a similar field of study

It Would Be Great If You Also Had

Experience with billing processes and system integrations/implementations; understanding of revenue recognition, invoicing, and reconciliation.
Familiarity with Zuora, NetSuite, Salesforce, Avalara (or a similar sales tax engine).
Understanding of subscription & usage based billing, and financial systems.

Aura is committed to offering a generous package to support our employees in all aspects of their life in and out of work. Our packages offer competitive pay, generous health and wellness benefits, retirement savings plans, parental leave and much more! Pay range for this position is $75,000–$90,000, but may vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, experience and location. This position is remote, but candidates must be US-based.

Analizar, integrar y transformar información de diferentes fuentes para generar insights, indicadores y herramientas de contro l
que permitan identificar desviaciones, inconsistencias, tendencias y oportunidades de mejora en la operación.

PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILIDADES

1 . Análisis y explotación de datos

Integrar, depurar y estructurar información proveniente de diferentes sistemas y fuentes.
Analizar grandes volúmenes de datos para identificar tendencias, patrones, desviaciones e inconsistencias.
Realizar cruces y conciliaciones entre información operativa, administrativa y financiera.
Diseñar análisis que permitan identificar causas, impactos y oportunidades de mejora.
Convertir datos en información útil para la toma de decisiones.

2. Validación y control de información

Validar la integridad, consistencia y calidad de las bases de datos utilizadas para el análisis.
Identificar duplicidades, errores, datos atípicos y diferencias entre fuentes.
Analizar la congruencia entre información solicitada, autorizada, ejecutada y facturada.
Dar seguimiento a excepciones y documentar hallazgos relevantes.

3. Análisis financiero aplicado

Analizar información de Cuentas por Pagar, gastos, facturación, presupuestos y centros de costo.
Aplicar conocimientos financieros para interpretar variaciones, costos, gastos y desviaciones.
Identificar posibles cargos improcedentes, diferencias o comportamientos atípicos.
Analizar información de proveedores y su comportamiento de facturación.
Evaluar el impacto económico de los hallazgos identificados.

4. Reportes, indicadores y visualización

Diseñar y mantener reportes, indicadores y dashboards para el seguimiento de la operación.
Automatizar procesos de extracción, transformación y análisis de información.
Presentar resultados mediante visualizaciones claras y orientadas a la toma de decisiones.
Comunicar hallazgos, tendencias, riesgos y recomendaciones a las áreas involucradas.

5. Mejora de procesos

Identificar oportunidades para automatizar y eficientar procesos de análisis y control.
Proponer nuevas fuentes de información, indicadores y metodologías de análisis.
Participar en proyectos de mejora relacionados con información operativa y financiera.

jobs.title: Market Data Analyst (459E6A7)
jobs.description:
Referment is working with a London-based financial technology company that supplies specialist credit data and analytics to some of the world's largest investment banks, asset managers and hedge funds. Its platform automatically structures bond and loan data across thousands of issuers in the US, Europe and emerging markets, giving credit teams auditable fundamentals on demand.

They are growing the market data team that owns the integrity of the bond and loan pricing and reference data behind their global credit product. As their new market data analyst, you will sit between the product and engineering teams, making sure the pricing data clients receive is right and building the automated checks that keep it right.

The Role

Review pricing feeds from a third-party pricing provider against internal benchmarks, investigating anomalies rather than accepting them.
Sift through large bond and loan price and reference datasets to identify, prioritise and resolve outliers, including tracing capital structures and inter-company relationships to keep aggregate-level data sound.
Calculate and validate bond and loan pricing data at scale, from YTM, YTW and z-spread to Macaulay and modified duration and PV01.
Build automated algorithms that reduce manual reviews and checks, and document or escalate recurring data quality issues to the pricing vendor and internal stakeholders.
Answer client questions about data and product functionality, working directly with leading investment firms.

What We're Looking For

Experience in evaluated pricing, independent price verification (IPV), fixed income valuations or trade support, or credit fund NAV pricing, for example as an investment bank IPV or vendor-side pricing analyst.
Strong familiarity with bond and loan reference data syntax and pricing feed structures, and command of pricing conventions (clean versus dirty price, accrued interest, day count) so you can sanity-check a price against its fundamentals.
Advanced Excel or Google Sheets skills, including complex spreadsheets with macros or Apps Script; Python, SQL or similar coding experience is a plus.
A demonstrated ability to work through large, messy datasets to find the one wrong number that everyone else's process missed.
A strong academic track record and sharp analytical and quantitative reasoning; an understanding of simple and complex corporate capital structures is useful.

This could suit an IPV, evaluated pricing or fixed income operations analyst at a large bank or data vendor who wants more ownership, a faster pace and the chance to automate the checks they currently run by hand. The role is permanent, full time and hybrid, based in London, with remote working flexibility offered by the company.

jobs.title: RCI-ABBV-35573 Technical Project Manager / Scrum Master (JIRA/Confluence/Dashboard/Sprint Metrics)
jobs.description:
Remote, must be able to work PST hours

Daily Work Schedule Expectations : 9am-2pm PST

Manager's Update:

This is not a traditional end-to-end Technical Program Manager role
and the candidate will not own the overall delivery timeline across an entire cross-functional program.

Role Focus:
Approximately 80% Scrum/Agile + 20% Technical Project Management
Core Responsibilities
Act as Scrum Master / Team Steward for three engineering teams
.
Lead and facilitate Scrum ceremonies across multiple teams running two-week sprints
.
Manage Scrum cadence and ensure ceremonies are conducted consistently and effectively.
Facilitate planning, stand-ups, retrospectives, reviews and other Agile ceremonies.
Help teams with prioritization and facilitate the flow of work.
Maintain visibility into team-level timelines, dependencies and project status.
Track approximately 3–4 projects of varying sizes across the three teams
at any given time.
Provide continuous reporting on team health, performance and delivery.
Use JIRA extensively
for task management, reporting and software-development metrics.
Work with Confluence
for documentation.
Participate in program meetings and provide status updates for the projects being executed by the assigned teams.
Maintain a high-fidelity understanding of the major technical projects being executed by each team.
Understand and operate within a structured Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC)
.
Coordinate effectively across engineering teams where initiatives have cross-team dependencies.

Engineering Environment
The individual will support three engineering teams:
Data Engineering Team

Largest team
Approximately 8 individual contributors + manager
Data engineering is a major component of the work.

AI / Machine Learning Team

Works on neural networks and related AI/ML initiatives.

Additional Engineering Team

Smaller team of approximately 3–4 people.

The candidate does not need to be an AI/ML or Data Engineering SME
, but exposure to these areas is a strong advantage.
Must-Have / High-Priority Experience
1. Strong hands-on Scrum experience – MUST HAVE

Proven experience serving as a Scrum Master, Agile Delivery Lead, Agile Project Manager or similar.
Has personally led Scrum ceremonies
, rather than simply working in a Scrum environment.
Experience supporting multiple engineering/software development teams
.
Comfortable working with two-week sprint cadences.
Experience facilitating ceremonies and helping teams maintain delivery discipline.

2. Strong JIRA proficiency – VERY IMPORTANT

Gerald specifically emphasized a high level of JIRA proficiency.
Candidate should be extremely comfortable using JIRA as a software-development task management and reporting platform.
Experience with JIRA reporting, dashboards, sprint tracking, metrics and team health/performance is highly valuable.

3. Technical/Software Development Environment

Good understanding of SDLC.
Experience working directly with software engineering teams.
Ability to understand technical projects at the team level without necessarily being the technical SME.
Experience with engineering project status, dependencies and delivery tracking.

4. Technical Project Management

Must understand project timelines and status for their assigned engineering teams.
Should be able to communicate project status in program meetings.
The candidate will own the timeline/status for their team's component
, not the entire cross-team program.

Strong Nice-to-Haves
Data Engineering

Previous experience working with data engineering teams or data engineering projects is highly desirable.

AI / ML

Exposure to AI, machine learning, neural networks or LLM-related engineering projects is a strong advantage.

Atlassian

JIRA is highly important.
Confluence experience is preferred.
Broader Atlassian Suite experience is a plus.

AI Automation / Development

Interest or experience in using AI to build automations, skills or workflows is a plus.
Exposure to tools such as Cloud Code / CodePilot or similar AI-assisted development/automation environments is beneficial.
Experience building AI-powered automations is a differentiator, but not a core requirement
.

Ideal Experience Level
Gerald specifically indicated that the sweet spot is approximately 5–8 years of experience
because of the complexity of the environment.
3–5 years
could work for a more traditional software-development environment, but for this particular role Gerald feels 5–8 years is the ideal range
.
Candidates with 15+ years
are not automatically rejected, but they need to genuinely be comfortable with the scope and understand that this role has limited ownership compared with senior/principal-level Technical Program Management positions.
Important Red Flags
Avoid candidates who are:
Primarily Senior/Staff/Principal Technical Program Managers
accustomed to owning large programs end-to-end.
Used to having significant strategic/program-level ownership and decision-making authority.
Expecting to own an initiative from inception through final delivery.
Primarily Product Managers
rather than Scrum/Agile practitioners.
Primarily Agile Transformation Consultants or Enterprise Agile Coaches.
Highly focused on Agile transformation, organizational change or coaching rather than hands-on Scrum execution.
Candidates who may become frustrated by a structured, process-heavy pharmaceutical environment.
Candidates whose Scrum experience is only theoretical or certification-based without actually leading ceremonies.
Candidates with no meaningful JIRA experience.

Agile Coaching Clarification
Gerald specifically stated that deep Agile transformation/coaching experience is NOT required
.
The organization currently uses Scrum primarily as a framework and is still developing its broader Agile mindset. Therefore, a candidate who is heavily focused on Agile transformation may not be the best match.
The priority is:
Hands-on Scrum execution > Agile transformation/coaching

Technical PM vs. Scrum Master Split
Gerald estimated the role at approximately:
80% – Scrum Master / Agile responsibilities

20% – Technical Project Management

The Technical PM component is primarily focused on:
Understanding team-level project timelines
Tracking team deliverables
Understanding project status
Communicating status
Managing team-level dependencies
Understanding what each engineering team is executing

The candidate is NOT responsible for the overall program timeline
when multiple teams/repos are involved.

Top 3 – 5 Skills Needed for each role

Experience leading agile/scrum ceremonies for multiple teams
Proficiency to expert level experience in Atlassian tools for task management (Jira, Confluence)
Prior experience and familiarity working with data engineering and AI/ML engineering teams in software development/delivery.
Technical project management experience on mid to large scale software projects.
(nice to have) Hands on experience with AI tools such as Claude code and Copilot.

Agile Specialist

As the Agile Specialist, you will report to the Senior Manager, Agile Practices as well as continuously collaborate with key stakeholders across the business to solve the most important technical problems.
You Will:

Lead and refine continuous planning, ensuring ongoing planning for and visibility to a rolling quarter + plan for the team/s you support.
Maintain engineering team schedules, ensuring proper resource planning and translation of estimates to key milestone dates.
Track project milestones, dependencies, deliverables, and timelines to ensure projects and programs stay on track and meet delivery timelines.
Remove obstacles that may hinder the team's progress.
Coordinate communication between different teams, departments, and stakeholders.
Collaborate with Engineering, Product, and PMO to manage and prioritize the product backlog.
Ensure engineers have necessary product requirements and UX designs to stay on track and meet deadlines.
Serve as the key liaison between software development teams and external stakeholders building advocacy and credibility.
Facilitate Agile ceremonies such as daily stand-ups, sprint planning, backlog maintenance and refinement, sprint reviews, and retrospectives.
Promote Agile best practices and educate team members to enhance team performance and productivity.
Support the JIRA management for teams they support and other tools as appropriate.
Provide burndown charts, velocity tracking, and other agile performance metrics to inform and resolve issues with the team and manager(s).

Required Experience & Skills:

Bachelor's degree in Business, Information Technology, or related field.
5+ years’ experience in an Agile environment with experience using Agile methodologies such as Scrum or Kanban.
Excellent organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional teams.
Strong problem-solving skills and adaptability.
Proficiency in JIRA, Confluence, and related tooling.

You will bring cross-functional partners together to create a fact-based view of current processes, identify waste and bottlenecks, and design a practical future state.

VSM Planning and Leadership:

Future-State Design:
Facilitate the development and documentation of a practical future-state process, including proposed process changes, roles, controls, technology needs, and enabling capabilities.

Continuous Improvement:

jobs.title: Revenue Operations Analyst
jobs.description:
About Us

At Botrista, we are revolutionizing beverage culture with intuitive, Nature-guided drink-making technology. By empowering restaurants and establishments to expand their menus without added complexity, we are driving growth and innovation at the touch of a button. Awarded as one of the Best California Startups in 2023, our solutions create a new industry category, applicable to any cuisine, demographic, and business. With rapid deployment of our machines nationwide, we are delivering extraordinary beverage experiences to customers everywhere.

Position Summary

Botrista is seeking a highly analytical and commercially minded Revenue Operations Analyst to help us better understand what drives revenue growth, customer performance, retention, and profitability across the business.

Reporting to the Revenue Operations Manager, this role will serve as a shared analytical resource across Revenue Operations, Commercial Planning, and Finance. The Revenue Analyst will connect data across Sales, Account Management, customer performance, deployments, operations, and financial results to identify trends, explain performance, uncover opportunities and risks, and support better business decisions.

This is not simply a reporting role. We are looking for someone who is naturally curious, comfortable digging into complex data, and able to move beyond what happened to understand why it happened and what we should do about it.

The ideal candidate combines strong analytical and technical skills with commercial judgment and can translate complex analysis into clear, actionable insights for business leaders.

Requirements

Key Responsibilities

Revenue Performance & Business Analysis

Analyze revenue performance against plan and identify the underlying drivers of variances.
Evaluate new customer revenue, recurring ingredient revenue, same-store performance, customer retention, expansion, cups sold daily (CSD), deployments, and other key revenue drivers.
Develop cohort and segmentation analyses across verticals, customer types, sales channels, territories, deal structures, acquisition sources, and other relevant dimensions.
Identify emerging trends, risks, anomalies, and growth opportunities before they become obvious in topline results.
Partner with Revenue Operations, Commercial Planning, and Finance to develop a consistent view of commercial and financial performance.
Translate analysis into clear recommendations and business actions.

Sales Analytics

Analyze pipeline health, coverage, conversion, sales velocity, win/loss performance, quota attainment, and seller productivity.
Evaluate lead sources, territories, customer segments, ICP performance, and sales motions.
Support analysis of sales capacity, territory design, quotas, and resource allocation.
Measure the downstream quality of customers acquired by Sales, including deployment, utilization, recurring revenue, retention, and expansion.
Support deployment and revenue forecasting and analyze forecast accuracy over time.

Customer Revenue & Retention Analytics

Analyze CSD, ingredient consumption, recurring revenue, account health, attrition, and expansion across the installed base.
Identify leading indicators of customer growth and churn risk.
Develop customer cohorts and account segmentation to identify which characteristics correlate with strong long-term performance.
Analyze Account Management interventions to determine which activities actually improve customer revenue, retention, and expansion.
Help develop data-driven account prioritization and opportunity/risk scoring.
Quantify revenue at risk and potential revenue upside across the existing customer base.

Customer Economics & Revenue Quality

Help develop a holistic view of customer value across the full lifecycle:

Sale → Deployment → Live → Productive → Recurring Revenue → Retention → Expansion

Evaluate customer economics across verticals, deal structures, sales channels, customer profiles, and other meaningful segments.
Partner with Finance to incorporate margin, cost, and profitability considerations into commercial analysis.
Identify customer and program characteristics associated with higher long-term economic value.
Help the organization move beyond measuring success solely by sales or installations toward measuring the quality and durability of revenue created.

Forecasting, Planning & Scenario Modeling

Support commercial revenue and deployment forecasting.
Build and maintain analytical models for revenue growth, customer performance, capacity, retention, and other business drivers.
Partner with Commercial Planning and Finance on operating plans, forecasts, and scenario analysis.
Evaluate the expected impact of changes in headcount, productivity, pricing, customer mix, retention, CSD, deployment timing, and other key assumptions.
Perform sensitivity analyses to help leadership understand the range of potential business outcomes.

Reporting & Business Reviews

Build and maintain core Sales, Account Management, and revenue performance reporting.
Support weekly and monthly business reviews with analysis of key trends, exceptions, risks, and opportunities.
Maintain consistent metric definitions and help establish a trusted source of truth across Revenue Operations, Commercial Planning, and Finance.
Improve existing reporting by eliminating low-value metrics and introducing measures that better reflect business performance.
Automate recurring analysis and reporting wherever practical.

Strategic & Ad Hoc Analysis

Support leadership with analytical work on high-priority business questions, including:

Which customer segments and verticals generate the greatest long-term value?
What predicts high CSD, recurring revenue, retention, and expansion?
Where are we losing revenue and why?
Which sales motions and acquisition sources produce the highest-quality customers?
Where should we add or reduce Sales and Account Management resources?
Which programs and initiatives are generating measurable incremental value?
Where are operational bottlenecks limiting revenue?
Which parts of the business should we scale, improve, or reconsider?
What are we not currently measuring that could materially change how we operate?

Cross-Functional Operating Model

The Revenue Analyst will be a shared analytical resource across Revenue Operations, Commercial Planning, and Finance.

The role reports to the Revenue Operations Manager, who will help prioritize the analyst's overall workload and ensure analytical work translates into commercial action. However, the analyst will work directly and regularly with Commercial Planning and Finance and will support important analytical and planning needs across all three functions.

Success requires operating as part of one analytical ecosystem rather than three separate teams. The expectation is to create shared definitions, shared data, and a common understanding of business performance while bringing the appropriate functional perspective to each analysis.

What Success Looks Like

A Successful Revenue Analyst Will

Surface insights leadership did not already know.
Explain the drivers behind business performance rather than simply reporting results.
Identify revenue opportunities and risks early enough for the organization to act.
Improve confidence in the metrics used to run the business.
Connect Sales and operational activity to actual customer and financial outcomes.
Reduce manual reporting and increase time spent on higher-value analysis.
Help Revenue Operations, Commercial Planning, and Finance operate from a consistent view of the business.
Develop a deep enough understanding of Botrista's business model to independently identify questions worth investigating.
Consistently move from data → insight → recommendation.

Qualifications

3+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Sales Operations, Business Analytics, Finance, Strategy, Business Operations, or a related analytical role.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with demonstrated ability to work with large and complex datasets.
Advanced Excel and/or Google Sheets skills.
Experience with Salesforce data and CRM reporting strongly preferred.
Experience with BI and data visualization tools preferred.
Experience building financial, operational, forecasting, or scenario models.
Strong understanding of business metrics and ability to connect operational activity to financial outcomes.
Ability to communicate complex analysis clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Strong attention to detail without losing sight of the larger business question.
Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where priorities and business questions evolve quickly.

What We're Looking For

We Are Particularly Interested In Someone Who

Is intellectually curious and naturally asks "why?"
Enjoys finding patterns and anomalies in data.
Does not stop at producing a dashboard or spreadsheet.
Can distinguish correlation from meaningful business drivers.
Is comfortable challenging assumptions when the data suggests something different.
Can take an ambiguous business question and independently determine how to analyze it.
Understands that perfect data is rarely available and can make thoughtful recommendations while clearly communicating assumptions and limitations.
Wants their analysis to influence how a business actually operates.

Benefits

Fully company-paid Medical and 99% company-paid Dental and Vision Insurance
Flex PTO, 7 sick days, 14 holidays, Wellness Benefits, Cell Phone and Internet reimbursement, 401K

Salary Range: $80,000 - $100,000

Guide and mentor research interns
Communicate and work with internal and external collaborators.

Qualifications

Preferred

jobs.description:
We are hiring Global Capability Model (GCM) Project Manager – REMOTE (6 Positions).

Please let me know if you are interested or anyone who might be interested.

Client: Major Pharmaceutical Client

Position: Global Capability Model (GCM) Project Manager – REMOTE

Duration: 6+ months on W2

Location: REMOTE

Pay Rate: $60.00-$90.00/ Hr on W2 (depending on experience level ONLY)

_________________________________________________________________________________________

Job Description

Position Summary

R&D is establishing and scaling global development hubs in India and Poland as part of its Global Capability Model (GCM) transformation.
The program is building new R&D capabilities while simultaneously redesigning how work is organized, where capabilities are located, and how teams operate across the global R&D network.
The Functional GCM Project Management role will provide dedicated execution support to one or more R&D Functional Leaders. The role will help translate functional strategies and designs into executable workforce, change, onboarding, and transition plans and ensure that issues are identified and resolved before they disrupt implementation. The R&D GCM Lead will be the hiring manager for these positions and deploy the new team members to the R&D functions.
This is a hands-on role requiring strong project management, structured problem solving, and the ability to work across global functions, HR, Talent Acquisition, Finance, local site teams, and other GCM workstreams.
The role may be filled at different levels of seniority. Senior resources will lead the work with Functional GCM Leads and independently drive cross-functional execution. More junior resources will provide project management, analysis, and coordination support within the same areas of responsibility.

Key Responsibilities

1. Functional GCM Execution

Partner with Functional GCM Leads to translate approved functional strategies and organization designs into practical execution plans.
Maintain an integrated view of functional milestones, dependencies, decisions, risks, and issues across workforce build, change, onboarding, and transition activities.
Connect functional execution with the broader GCM program and identify dependencies requiring coordination across R&D functions, GCM sites, or enterprise teams.
Ensure emerging execution issues are surfaced early, with clear options and recommendations for resolution.

2. R&D HQ Transition Support and Hypercare

Establish and operate a high-touch transition support process for functions moving work, building new teams, or implementing new operating models.
Provide a clear point of coordination for transition issues raised by functional leaders, managers, and new teams.
Triage issues quickly, connect them to the appropriate owner, and drive follow-through until resolution.
Identify recurring issues and patterns that indicate broader gaps in processes, policies, onboarding, technology, or site readiness and escalate them through the GCM program.
The objective is not simply to track issues, but to remove friction and reduce execution risk during periods of significant organizational change.

3. Onboarding and Operational Readiness

Partner with Functional GCM Leads, hiring managers, and local India and Poland Knowledge Transfer PM teams to prepare for successful onboarding of new employees and teams.
Coordinate functional readiness for hiring cohorts, including manager preparation, local orientation, access and tools, role onboarding, and other dependencies required for employees to become productive.
Work closely with dedicated Knowledge Transfer PMs while maintaining clear separation between overall functional implementation and detailed knowledge-transfer execution.
Ensure dependencies between hiring, onboarding, knowledge transfer, and operational readiness are visible and managed.

4. Workforce and Hiring Planning

Support Functional GCM Leads in finalizing workforce and hiring plans, including roles, locations, timing, sequencing, and hiring waves.
Maintain accurate functional demand and hiring plans and reconcile changes with Talent Acquisition, HR, and the central GCM workforce planning process.
Track progress from approved workforce demand through requisition launch, recruiting, and hiring, highlighting risks to planned timing or workforce assumptions.
Help identify practical adjustments to sequencing, role profiles, or hiring plans when market conditions or execution performance differ from assumptions.

5. Change and Communications

Support development and execution of divisional and functional change and communication plans associated with GCM implementation.
Work with Functional GCM Leads, HR, and Communications to identify affected stakeholder groups, key messages, leadership engagement needs, manager support, and employee readiness activities.
Coordinate functional change activities with the broader R&D GCM narrative and site-level communications.
Track change readiness, emerging concerns, and adoption risks and ensure they are addressed through the appropriate functional or program channels.

6. Business Cases and Functional Design Support

Support development of business cases for new or evolving functional GCM designs.
Coordinate collection and analysis of workforce, cost, timing, organizational, and operational assumptions required to assess proposed designs.
Work with Functional GCM Leads, Finance, HR, and the broader GCM team to prepare materials for design reviews and investment decisions.
Maintain traceability between approved business-case assumptions and subsequent execution plans.

Seniority Differentiation

Senior Project Management Resource (1 or 2 in total)

In collaboration with the R&D GCM Program Lead and GCM PMO Lead, senior resources will:
Serve as the primary execution partner to one or more Functional GCM Leads.
Independently lead integrated functional planning and execution.
Drive resolution of complex cross-functional dependencies and issues.
Challenge assumptions and identify gaps in functional implementation plans.
Lead development of business cases, executive materials, and decision recommendations.
Facilitate senior stakeholder discussions and drive decisions to closure.
Direct and coordinate work performed by more junior project management resources, where applicable.
Represent the functional workstream in broader GCM governance and integration discussions.

Project Manager Resource (4–5 in total)

In collaboration with the R&D GCM Program Lead and R&D GCM PMO Lead, junior PM resources will:
Support development and maintenance of workforce, change, onboarding, and transition plans.
Coordinate meetings, inputs, actions, decisions, and dependencies across stakeholders.
Maintain accurate execution tracking and prepare status and decision materials.
Perform analysis supporting workforce plans, business cases, and implementation decisions.
Coordinate onboarding readiness and transition support activities.
Track risks and issues and drive follow-up with responsible owners.
Escalate emerging execution concerns to the senior PM or Functional GCM Lead.

Qualifications

Demonstrated project or program management experience in a complex, global organization.
Ability to manage multiple interconnected workstreams with significant organizational and stakeholder dependencies.
Strong analytical skills and ability to translate strategy or organization design into practical implementation plans.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including preparation of clear executive-level materials.
Ability to work effectively with senior functional leaders as well as operational teams.
Demonstrated ability to identify risks, resolve ambiguity, and drive issues to closure.
Experience with workforce planning, organizational transformation, change management, business-case development, or large-scale implementation preferred.
Experience within pharmaceutical R&D, life sciences, or another complex global operating environment preferred but not required.

Critical Capabilities

Successful candidates will be able to move comfortably between strategy and execution. They should be highly organized without becoming process-heavy, able to work through ambiguity, willing to challenge plans that are not executable, and effective at building relationships across functions and geographies.
They must be comfortable operating in an environment where design and execution are occurring simultaneously and where priorities, workforce assumptions, and implementation approaches will continue to evolve as the program progresses.

new_jobs.title: (Remote) Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Systems & Software, a division of Harris; is seeking a Project Manager

Systems and Software (www.ssivt.com), a division of Harris Computer Systems, is a software development company headquartered in Winooski, VT. S&S's single focus is on delivering horizontally and vertically scalable customer service solutions to the utility industry. Our reputation is one of market-leading software, exceptional solution delivery, and a customer-focused organization.

For a utility, a Customer Information System (CIS) is more than just a collection of records, it's a lifeline between the utility and its most important asset, its customers. From turn-on to move-out, no other system will have the impact on the customer experience that the CIS does, so ensuring that this solution offers the breadth of scope and responsiveness that modern consumers require is a critical priority. Through our flagship product, enQuesta, S&S meets this need for our electric, water, sewer and gas customers by combining an intuitive design with powerful technology. The enQuesta solution not only presents a modern, innovative face for the utility to the end customers, but also enables the utilities to take advantage of the solution's open architecture when developing future programs and initiatives.

This remote role welcomes candidates anywhere in Canada and the US. Travel is required as needed, approximately 75%. Candidates must hold a current, valid passport and be legally eligible to travel internationally. This includes either passport based visa exemption or possession of any required travel visas for entry into Canada, the United States, and the Caribbean. This opportunity can be performed remotely or from our office in Winooski, VT. Travel, depending on the project(s).

Salary

80K - 100K

AI & Innovation Mindset

We are committed to leveraging emerging technologies to improve how we work, serve our customers, and drive business outcomes. The successful candidate will demonstrate curiosity and a willingness to actively adopt and leverage AI tools to improve workflows, solve problems, and increase efficiency. Candidates should be comfortable using AI enabled technologies, including copilots, chat based AI assistants, and automation tools, as part of their everyday work while maintaining appropriate judgment, security, and compliance standards.

What Your Impact Will Be

Project Coordination & Management

Coordinate components of utility CIS software implementation projects, ensuring alignment with organizational goals.
Maintain and update detailed project plans, timelines, and budgets to ensure projects remain on track.
Identify and report issues, risks, or delays in a timely manner to the PMO Manager and stakeholders for resolution.
Provide clear communication and regular updates on project progress to the PMO Manager and project teams.

Process Support & Standardization

Assist the PMO Manager in maintaining project management documentation and processes to ensure consistency across projects.
Adhere to established project management methodologies, including Waterfall and Agile, and support continuous improvement initiatives.
Ensure compliance with project management practices and help identify areas for administrative efficiency.

Stakeholder Communication

Maintain consistent communication with internal teams, including R&D, Sales, and Delivery, to ensure alignment on project tasks.

Financial Tracking & Reporting

Assist in monitoring project budgets, ensuring expenses are tracked against financial goals.
Track and report on project status, timelines, and financials, generating regular status reports for the PMO Manager.
Collaborate with finance teams to verify financial data aligns with forecasts.

Performance Monitoring

Track key performance indicators (KPIs) such as project delivery timelines and budget variance.
Assist in analyzing project execution data to contribute ideas for enhancing team efficiency.
Support the PMO Manager in preparing project status updates and gathering data for issue escalation.
Participate in client-facing discussions, documenting meeting minutes and action items to ensure customer satisfaction.

What We Are Looking For

1-3 years of experience in project management or a related role, preferably within software implementations or technical environments.
Experience in managing project budgets ranging from $10k to over $2.5M.
Familiarity with project management tools such as Jira, Spira, Confluence, SharePoint, and Clarizen.
Basic understanding of Waterfall project management; exposure to Agile methodologies is a plus.
Experience tracking project financials or budgets is preferred.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to engage effectively with team members and customers.
Ability to work collaboratively and manage tasks with guidance.
Strong problem-solving abilities with a focus on learning and delivering results.
Experience working in a team-oriented environment, collaborating with cross-functional groups such as Sales, R&D, and Delivery.
Detail-oriented with a strong focus on organization and process.
Position may require travel as high as 75% in North America without restriction.
Frequent communication through Teams, phone calls, and email to stay connected with remote teams and leadership.

What We Can Offer

3 weeks’ vacation and 5 personal days
Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits starting from your first day of employment
Employee stock ownership and RRSP/401k matching programs
Lifestyle rewards
Remote work and more!

About Systems & Software

Systems & Software, a subsidiary of Harris Computer and part of Constellation Software, has been serving utilities and municipalities since 1973. Headquartered in Vermont, the company provides the enQuesta CIS platform to manage billing and utility operations for electric, water, gas, wastewater, solid waste, and property taxes. Our solutions enable utilities to manage complex rate structures, streamline operations, and enhance customer service, all without the need for custom code or disconnected systems. With cloud-based deployment, SOC 2 Type II certification, and interoperability with meter data systems, GIS, and financial tools, Systems & Software delivers stability, security, and flexibility that utilities can trust. Our commitment to ongoing investment ensures continuous innovation and a strong partnership with our customers across North America.

About Harris

Harris is a leading provider of mission critical software to the public sector in North America. As a wholly owned subsidiary of Constellation Software Inc. (“CSI”, symbol CSU on the TSX), Harris has become the cornerstone for CSI’s investment in utility, local government, school districts, public safety, and healthcare software verticals. Our success has been realized through investments in our proprietary software and market expertise. This focus, combined with acquiring businesses that build upon or complement our offerings, has helped drive our success. Harris will continue to growth through reinvestment – both in the people and products that we offer and making investments in acquiring new businesses.

Job Description

Timmons Group
is hiring a Senior Project Manager
to join our Geospatial Solutions Development division
, based in Richmond, VA or working remotely
. This position leads delivery for a long-standing state government client, a multi-year program with new development, enhancements, maintenance and support, and modernization all running at once. The position may also lead or support engagements for our other state, local, federal, and non-government clients.

The Senior Project Manager
is the primary client contact, advising on how to sequence and fund competing priorities, planning across overlapping timelines, and working with cross-functional teams to execute. The role also owns the financial side, including budgets, change orders, and monthly invoicing, and calls for enough technical depth to plan around architecture, integrations, data migrations, and releases. We welcome candidates from consulting firms and from state or local government who have managed technology projects and vendor partnerships.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities
include but are not limited to:

Serve as the primary point of contact for the client, from day-to-day coordination through executive status reviews
Advise the client on trade-offs and priorities across new development, enhancements, support, and modernization
Navigate difficult conversations early, including scope disputes, slipping dates, and funding constraints
Run an integrated plan across concurrent workstreams and sequence shared people and environments
Hold teams to commitments; unblock, escalate, and keep work moving
Fit the delivery approach (agile, predictive, or hybrid) to each workstream
Manage risks, issues, dependencies, and decisions
Partner with business analysts, engineers, QA, UX, and architects to build the backlog and release plan
Balance support and maintenance requests against planned project work, including SLA commitments
Coordinate releases, client UAT, and go-live readiness
Own budgets, burn, and forecasts for each contract and task order
Prepare monthly invoices and resolve billing questions with the client
Price and negotiate change orders and new statements of work
Lead or support additional client engagements as assigned

Skills/Requirements
of a successful candidate include but are not limited to:

Bachelor's degree in a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience
7+ years managing custom software delivery, including 5+ years on state government programs, from either the vendor or agency side; experience with GIS or location-based applications is a plus
Experience with natural resources or environmental agencies, or with local, federal, or private-sector clients, is desirable
Experience as the main link between an agency and its technology partners on multi-year programs
Experience running concurrent workstreams, including legacy modernization alongside ongoing support and enhancements, and sequencing shared people across them
Hands-on contract and financial management, including budgets, invoicing, change orders, and public-sector procurement
Fluency in agile, predictive, and hybrid delivery; PMP or agile certifications are desirable
Strong advisory and communication skills, with the tenacity to keep work moving through difficult situations
Comfort using AI tools in day-to-day work
Familiarity with Azure DevOps, Microsoft 365, Basecamp, and Smartsheet, or comparable tools

Our best estimate of the salary range for this position is $90,000-$140,000. There may be flexibility on salary for experienced candidates. new_jobs.description:
Posting Type

Remote

Job Overview

About Relativity

Legal technology is having its moment — and Relativity is at the center of it.

We are a leading legal data intelligence company. Our extensible, AI cloud platform, RelativityOne, is trusted by the world’s largest law firms, corporations, and government agencies to turn complex data into actionable insights for litigation, investigations, regulatory inquiries, arbitration, and other high-stakes legal matters.

In Asia, the momentum speaks for itself: RelativityOne adoption jumped 46% year-over-year, a sign that organisations have moved beyond experimentation and are now applying AI in product environments to modernise how legal work gets done at scale.

To meet this moment, we’re expanding our Singapore team and on-the-ground presence. This is an opportunity to be part of an exciting growth story. We are looking for mid-level professionals across sales, technical solutions, customer success, and marketing to support our continued expansion. You’ll have the backing of an established industry leader and the opportunity to help grow our customer base across Asia.

If you’re ready to help write the next chapter of legal AI in Asia, we’d love to hear from you.

Job Summary

Job Description and Requirements

This is an exceptional opportunity for an excellent hands-on marketing program manager to help build and drive growth for Relativity in dynamic markets. This is a high-impact, commercially focused role for a marketing lead who is as comfortable advising senior stakeholders as they are rolling up their sleeves to execute against plan.

As the Program Manager, Field Marketing — Asia, based in Singapore, you will own the development of the field marketing strategy and the delivery of marketing plans for the Asia region, with specific focus on Singapore, Hong Kong, India, and South Korea, with accountability for commercial outcomes in the region.

Drawing on deep knowledge of Asia customers, personas, and market dynamics — across four genuinely distinct markets — you will work with the APAC leadership to set the Asia regional marketing agenda, shape and deliver integrated marketing programs, generate regional campaigns and localising global ones to ensure maximum regional relevance, driving pipeline towards meeting aggressive revenue targets.

You will act as a trusted in-region marketing authority to sales leadership and senior stakeholders — translating business objectives into marketing plans, providing strategic counsel, and ensuring marketing is a true commercial driver to success. You will also collaborate closely with Australia, UK and US-based marketing teams, leveraging global capabilities to maximise resources, maintain brand consistency across the Asia region.

As an individual contributor, working in the wider APAC marketing team, you are proactive, driven and work effectively across functions and geographies, holding yourself and others to a high standard. You communicate with authority and clarity, thrive on ownership, and bring credibility and gravitas to influence at every level.

Job Responsibilities

Develop a comprehensive field marketing strategy aligned to regional business priorities and revenue goals, spanning the full customer journey — from awareness through to pipeline acceleration and retention — with a coherent, locally relevant go-to-market narrative at their core.
Plan, manage, and deliver integrated marketing programs including in-person events, executive roundtables, webinars, and third-party activations.
Acts as a senior in-region marketing authority to key stakeholders — advising on marketing strategy and plans, and ensuring alignment between marketing activities and business priorities.
Lead end-of-the-end program management, including timelines, budgets, vendors, and logistics, ensuring delivery on time and within scope.
Serves as the in-region authority for all Asia events — including owning the regional presence at RelFest Sydney and flagship Asia events — leading audience acquisition campaigns, driving registrations and attendance goals, developing supporting content, and building event awareness across the region.
Manages joint marketing relationships with third-party sponsors and channel partners to drive in-market awareness, generate pipeline, and deliver against shared commercial goals.
Amplifies global marketing initiatives to ensure messaging resonates with local audiences, adapting content, channels, and positioning for local relevance. Localises content for Asia audiences and personas.
Collaborates cross-functionally with Demand Generation, Product Marketing, Brand, and Marketing Operations to ensure consistent messaging and campaign integration.
Partners with the global content team to execute against the regional content strategy, including the creation of customer success.
Serves as a trusted marketing partner to the in-market sales teams, keeping them informed of programme plans, campaign updates, and access to promotional materials, and building strong relationships that make marketing an integral part of commercial success.
Sets, tracks, and reports on campaign metrics and commercial KPIs; translates performance data into actionable insights and continually optimises programmes to improve outcomes and maximise ROI.
Be accountable for marketing’s contribution to pipeline generation, revenue contribution, and commercial outcomes in market.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) in marketing or a related field
7+ years professional experience in marketing, with a track record of owning commercial outcomes in a senior field marketing or demand generation role.
Proven in-market experience across at least one Asia market (Singapore, Hong Kong, India, or South Korea)

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working in B2B technology or SaaS marketing environments with experience across more than one Asia market: Singapore, Hong Kong, India, or South Korea
Familiarity with marketing automation and CRM platforms (e.g., Marketo, Salesforce)

new_jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager I
new_jobs.description:
Join Axon and be a Force for Good.

At Axon, we’re on a mission to Protect Life. We’re explorers, pursuing society’s most critical safety and justice issues with our ecosystem of devices and cloud software. Like our products, we work better together. We connect with candor and care, seeking out diverse perspectives from our customers, communities and each other.

Life at Axon is fast-paced, challenging and meaningful. Here, you’ll take ownership and drive real change. Constantly grow as you work hard for a mission that matters at a company where you matter.

Location: Germany

Travel:
up to 40% within DACH, Benelux, Nordics (an other European countries as needed)
Reports to:
Director, Professional Services, EMEA

Your Impact

As a Senior Technical Project Manager, you’ll lead high-visibility projects, directly contributing to the development and implementation of solutions that truly make a difference. In this role, you’ll tackle complex challenges, working with some of the most advanced technologies in the industry, including cloud and on-prem platforms, and mission-critical systems. You’ll have the opportunity to collaborate with brilliant minds across professional services, sales, engineering, product, and customer teams to deliver solutions that save lives and enhance public trust.
At Axon, we’re driven by a powerful mission: to protect life, capture truth, and accelerate justice. We’re growing rapidly, and this is your chance to make a lasting impact at a company where innovation meets purpose.

What You’ll Do

Program & Project Management

Manage all aspects of complex enterprise-grade product deployments
Oversee project milestones, resource planning, scope, timeline, and risk management.
Manage cross-functional stakeholders to ensure alignment, transparency, and on-time delivery.
Ensures project milestones and deadlines are met and associated documentation supports customer acceptance for purposes of revenue recognition
Support pre-sales scoping and post-sales implementation handoff.
Operates with a sense of urgency, accuracy, and detail-orientation, while maintaining consistent lines of communication with all teams involved in each project
Maintain customer confidence, especially in high-pressure situations
Remain organized and focused on removing obstacles through creativity and adaptation to rapidly changing circumstances

Partner Management

Own the relationship with 3rd party integrator and the client throughout the length of the contract

Stakeholder Collaboration

Work closely with Professional Services, Product Managers, and Engineers to align program execution with business goals.
Act as a liaison between customers and internal teams to manage change requests, solution feasibility, and roadmap alignment.

Process Improvement

Identify process inefficiencies and propose improvements to increase deployment speed, quality, and customer satisfaction.
Contribute to internal SOPs, implementation playbooks, and best practices.

What You Bring

Fluency in both German and English
European citizenship is required in order to work with sensitive Government data, willing to undergo a security check
5+ years of experience leading and delivering highly complex programs, with demonstrated success in technical program management.
Proven track record of managing enterprise-level software deployments, infrastructure projects, or large-scale enterprise application programs.
Deep expertise in delivering complex projects involving cross-functional teams, including sales, engineering, and product.
Mastery of program/project management tools and methodologies to track, report, and deliver on objectives. (PMP, PRINCE2, SCRUM)
Experience gathering requirements, optimizing workflows, and facilitating change management within teams.
Familiarity with software configurations and coding experience (particularly JSON) preferred.
Advanced communication and presentation skills, with the ability to distill technical concepts for diverse audiences.
Proficiency in guiding client and internal teams through ambiguity, driving alignment, and executing on shared goals.

Don’t meet every single requirement? That's ok. At Axon, we Aim Far. We think big with a long-term view because we want to reinvent the world to be a safer, better place. We are also committed to building diverse teams that reflect the communities we serve.

If you’re excited about this role and our mission to Protect Life but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with every qualification listed here, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

new_jobs.title: Regional Program Manager - Portland Metro
new_jobs.description:
POSITION TYPE:
Full-time, exempt; some evening and weekend work required
LOCATION:
Portland metropolitan area; hybrid, with regular work in schools and community settings throughout the region and occasional statewide travel
REPORTS TO:
Director of Education 
START DATE:
Dec 1, 2026
APPLICATION DEADLINE:
Open until filled with priority given to applicants who apply by October 20, 2026. 

CLP is looking for a relationship-builder, community educator, and connector who believes powerful civic learning happens both inside and outside the classroom. The Portland Regional Program Manager will build partnerships among educators, schools, students, community-based organizations, civic institutions, and local leaders throughout the Portland metropolitan area.
This position is designed for someone whose experience crosses traditional boundaries: a community organizer who has worked closely with schools and young people, a nonprofit leader with teaching experience, an educator who has organized communities, or another professional who knows how to bring people together around shared civic-learning goals.
You will not simply deliver programs created elsewhere. You will listen to educators and communities, identify local assets and needs, adapt and deliver CLP programs, and help develop approaches that reflect Portland-area schools and communities. Throughout this work, you will uphold CLP's commitment to nonpartisanship and help create learning environments in which people with different perspectives and backgrounds can participate constructively.

THE ROLE'S THREE CORE PRIORITIES

Build trusted relationships and community partnerships that strengthen civic learning opportunities for students and educators.
Support educators in meeting the goals of Oregon Senate Bill 513 by connecting required civics instruction with meaningful classroom learning and engagement with Portland-area civic institutions and communities.
Develop, implement, and evaluate regional programs and pilots that expand access to high-quality civic learning and inform CLP’s statewide work.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Community Organizing and Partnership Development

Build trusted partnerships: Develop sustained relationships with schools, culturally and geographically diverse community organizations, youth-serving organizations, civic institutions, local government, legal professionals, and other Portland-area partners.
Community Engagement: Engage educators, students, and community partners to identify local needs, assets, barriers, and opportunities in developing and delivering programming.
Build coalitions: Bring together people and organizations that may not ordinarily work together around the shared goal of strengthening students' civic knowledge, skills, and participation.
Develop community leadership: Recruit, prepare, and support community members to serve as volunteers, speakers, mentors, content experts, and partners in student civic-learning experiences.
Expand access: Identify Portland-area schools, educators, and communities that have had less access to CLP programming and develop relationship-based strategies to increase participation.
Lead regional relationships: Build CLP's presence in education, civic, and community networks and represent CLP at meetings, events, convenings, and professional-learning opportunities.

Educator Partnership and Civic Learning

Support educators: Provide curricular consultation, in-classroom assistance when appropriate, volunteer matching, and follow-through tailored to educators' needs and school contexts.
Connect classrooms and communities: Create opportunities for students to learn with community leaders and explore local legal, civic, and public-policy questions through inquiry and experiential learning.
Facilitate professional learning: Design and lead workshops, teacher cohorts, and other learning opportunities that support implementation of CLP programs, Oregon civics standards, and SB 513.
Adapt CLP programs: Help schools implement programs such as Community Action Projects, Mock Trial, Courthouse Tours, and other CLP offerings in ways that are practical, relevant, and nonpartisan.

Regional Program Development, Delivery, and Learning

Co-design responsive programming: Work with CLP’s Education Team and regional partners to develop student-centered programming that supports implementation of Oregon Senate Bill 513 and is grounded in community knowledge, local resources, and educator needs.
Lead regional pilots: Plan, implement, and refine pilot programs that test community-rooted approaches to strengthening civic learning and collaboration among educators, students, and community partners.
Coordinate events and civic learning experiences: Develop and support tours, conferences, workshops, and other student- and educator-centered programs that connect classroom civics instruction with civic and legal institutions and help educators create meaningful learning experiences aligned with Oregon’s civics requirements.
Manage projects and partnerships: Develop work plans, coordinate logistics, monitor timelines and budgets, and maintain clear communication with internal and external partners supporting regional civic learning.
Use evidence to improve: Collect participant feedback and program data; maintain accurate records in CLP’s CRM; and use findings to strengthen programs, assess how CLP is supporting educators and students under SB 513, and inform statewide learning.
Communicate opportunities: Develop clear, engaging regional communications that connect educators, volunteers, and partners with CLP programs and resources that support high-quality civics instruction.

YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU...

Are comfortable working across political, geographic, cultural, and institutional differences while maintaining nonpartisanship.
Can operate comfortably in board rooms, classrooms, courtrooms, and community spaces.
Enjoys working with both educators and community members.
Know how to listen to a community before proposing a solution.
Are energized by bringing people and organizations together across different priorities and perspectives.
Can translate broad ideas about democracy and civic participation into practical opportunities for young people.
Enjoy building and improving programs, while also administering established ones.

Minimum Qualifications

At least five years of combined professional experience in community organizing, K-12 education, youth development, nonprofit programming, community engagement, or a closely related field.
Meaningful experience working in both education and community organizing, coalition building, or partnership development.
Demonstrated ability to build trusting relationships across communities, institutions, and organizations with different priorities and perspectives.
Experience facilitating groups and communicating effectively with educators, young people, volunteers, community partners, and civic leaders.
Knowledge of interactive, experiential, project-based, or place-based learning strategies.
Ability to manage multiple projects with attention to relationships, timelines, budgets, details, and follow-through.
Familiarity with Portland-area schools, districts, education organizations, community-based organizations, and/or civic institutions.
Ability to navigate complex institutional environments while maintaining CLP's commitment to nonpartisanship.
Strong writing, collaboration, judgment, and organizational skills.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and Google Workspace.
Residence in the Portland metropolitan area, a valid driver's license and auto insurance, and reliable transportation for regional travel.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working at the intersection of education and community engagement, with familiarity with K–12 schools, educators, students, or youth-serving programs.
Experience with CLP programs or similar student-centered civic-education initiatives.
Established relationships within Portland-area education, youth-development, community, or civic networks.
Experience engaging communities through listening sessions, outreach, volunteer engagement, coalition building, or community-based programming.
Experience in legal, judicial, local-government, or public-policy settings.
Experience with CRM and project-management systems; familiarity with Virtuous, VOMO, Canva, Asana, or Slack is helpful.

Interested but not sure you meet every qualification? We encourage you to apply.

TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT AND COMPENSATION

Salary range: $65,000-$72,000 annually, based on experience.
Status: Full-time (40 hours per week), exempt employee.
Schedule: Work generally occurs Monday through Friday in a hybrid environment. Hours are flexible to meet the needs of educators and community partners. Some evening and weekend work is required for meetings, programs, and events.
Benefits: Competitive benefits package including full medical, dental, and vision insurance for the employee; long-term disability and life insurance; and a 403(b) retirement plan with a 3% employer contribution after six months of continuous employment.
Employment requirements: Employment is contingent upon a background check and verification of employment eligibility. Regional travel requires a valid driver's license, auto insurance, and reliable transportation.

Civics Learning Project is an equal opportunity employer. CLP does not discriminate in employment, educational programs, or activities on any basis protected by applicable law.

TO APPLY

Please submit the following materials:
Cover letter: Describe how your experience in education and community organizing or partnership development prepares you for the Portland Regional Program Manager role.
Resume: Clearly describe experience relevant to the position.
References: Provide three professional references, including at least one - preferably two - current or former supervisors.

Email materials as PDFs to employment@civicslearning.org with "Portland RPM" in the subject line. All inquiries will be handled confidentially.

Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. Position Summary

Analog Devices' Software & Digital Platforms (SDP) group is seeking an experienced Senior Program Manager with deep embedded software experience to oversee complex programs for next-generation MCU, DSP, and SoC products. The successful candidate will lead programs across the full product development lifecycle, spanning firmware, Linux and Zephyr software stacks, device drivers, Common HAL, ROM and boot software, BSPs, SDKs, middleware, security enablement, low-level I/O, and SoC/MCU platform development.

This role will work closely with SDP's Linux Factory, Zephyr Factory, ROM, Security, Common HAL, Unified SDK, and platform software organizations to ensure scalable, reusable, and high-quality software deliverables across multiple product families and business units. The candidate will drive disciplined execution and alignment between embedded software, silicon design, hardware engineering, validation, systems, applications, and customer-facing teams.

This position requires strong technical understanding of embedded systems and semiconductor development, exceptional leadership, a proactive management approach, and the ability to collaborate across highly technical, multi-disciplinary global teams. ADI thrives on positive, transparent, and solutions-oriented engagement, and this role requires exactly that.

Job Requirements

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.
10-15 years of hands-on Program Management, Project Management, or Technical Program Management experience managing embedded software programs, firmware platforms, silicon enablement programs, or semiconductor development initiatives.
Experience working in semiconductor industry required
Strong technical foundation with experience in several of the following:

Embedded Software and Platform Technologies

Firmware and driver development (Linux, Zephyr, Bare-Metal, HAL).
RTOS technologies including Zephyr, FreeRTOS, ThreadX, embOS, or VxWorks.
Linux kernel drivers, BSP development, device trees, Yocto/OpenEmbedded environments, and embedded Linux release processes.
Bootloaders, ROM software, secure boot chains, silicon initialization, and low-level peripheral drivers.
Power and clock management, SoC initialization, hardware bring-up, and platform enablement.
Common HAL, middleware, SDKs, reusable software frameworks, and software platform architectures.
Developer tools, SDK infrastructure, CI/CD pipelines, software release governance, and software quality frameworks.

Semiconductor and System Experience

Experience working with MCUs, SoCs, ASICs, DSPs, wireless chipsets, PMICs, mixed-signal products, edge AI systems, or automotive controllers.
Strong understanding of semiconductor development lifecycles, silicon readiness milestones, and post-silicon validation workflows.
Understanding of New Product Introduction (NPI) processes for combined silicon and firmware programs.

Program Leadership

Demonstrated leadership, decision making, teamwork, interpersonal, and communication skills with a proven track record leading large multi-disciplinary engineering teams across multiple geographies and time zones.
Hands-on engineering background with prior experience developing firmware, writing drivers, integrating RTOS platforms, designing silicon blocks, or contributing to hardware board or system design.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to solve complex technical and organizational problems through structured experimentation and data-driven decision making.
Proficiency with modern program management and engineering tools including MS Project, Jira, Confluence, Jama Connect, Azure DevOps, and software lifecycle management systems.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to translate technical and program information for audiences ranging from engineers to executive leadership.
Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities, complex dependencies, and aggressive delivery schedules.

Platform and Factory Enablement Experience

Experience working with software platform organizations responsible for Linux, Zephyr, ROM, SDK, security, tooling, or reusable software infrastructure.
Familiarity with factory-based software development models focused on standardization, scalability, reuse, developer productivity, and release quality.
Understanding of open-source development practices, upstream contribution strategies, and community engagement models.
Positive attitude, self-motivated, proactive, accountable, and results-oriented.

Additional Preferred Skills

Experience leading or supporting Linux Factory, Zephyr Factory, ROM, Security, Common HAL, Unified SDK, HDL Factory, or software platform initiatives.
Experience managing reusable software platforms deployed across multiple product lines and business units.
Experience with customer-facing technical roles supporting embedded software, Linux solutions, RTOS products, silicon platforms, or SDK ecosystems.
Familiarity with product security requirements, secure software development lifecycle practices, and firmware security architectures.
Experience with ASPICE, Functional Safety, ISO 26262, IEC 61508, CMMI, or similar process and quality frameworks.
PMP, PMI-ACP, Scrum Master, SAFe, or equivalent certifications.
Experience coordinating globally distributed engineering teams.
Willingness to travel occasionally as needed.

Own and drive large-scale embedded software, platform enablement, and silicon-related programs to meet scope, schedule, budget, quality, and business objectives.
Lead Agile program execution processes while collaborating closely with firmware, Linux, Zephyr, ROM, Common HAL, security, silicon design, hardware engineering, validation, systems, applications, and customer support teams.
Drive alignment between software platform roadmaps and product delivery schedules to maximize reuse and accelerate time-to-market.
Coordinate execution across Linux Factory, Zephyr Factory, ROM, Security, Common HAL, Unified SDK, and product-focused engineering organizations.
Drive alignment between firmware and silicon milestones including ES samples, EVT, DVT, PVT, first silicon bring-up, validation readiness, and production release.

Drive retrospectives, lessons learned activities, and process improvements across all technical disciplines.

Provide clear and concise program reporting to engineering leadership and executive stakeholders.
