Overview

Are you an experienced project leader who can build trusted client relationships, lead multidisciplinary teams and deliver critical outcomes across complex, highly regulated nuclear programmes?

We're looking for Principal / Chief Project Managers to lead some of Reactor Operations' most important work for our core clients: EDF, Rolls-Royce Submarines, Urenco and Westinghouse. Our teams support EDF's'operating nuclear fleet through generation, life extension, defuelling and the transition towards decommissioning; help Rolls-Royce Submarines design, manufacture and sustain the reactor plants that support the UK's Defence Nuclear Enterprise; and deliver engineering, safety, infrastructure and project solutions for Urenco and Westinghouse across the nuclear fuel cycle. We also support the broader Atkinsrealis business across defence, new build, decommissioning, fusion and net zero initiatives.

As a Principal / Chief Project Manager, you'll be at the heart of these long-term client partnerships. You'll shape delivery strategies, lead complex projects and programmes, bring together our technical capabilities and create the confidence, clarity and commercial discipline needed to deliver safely and successfully. You'll also help identify what our clients need next, strengthen our strategic relationships and support the continued growth of Reactor Operations.

Your role

You'll combine project leadership, commercial judgement, client engagement and strategic thinking to deliver complex engineering projects and programmes.

Depending on your experience and the scale of the role, you'll:

Lead complex projects, programmes or portfolios for our core clients, establishing clear outcomes and creating the conditions for safe, high-quality and predictable delivery.
Build trusted relationships with senior clients and stakeholders, developing a deep understanding of their operational, programme and strategic priorities and longer-term needs.
Translate complex client requirements into clear delivery strategies, integrated plans and measurable outcomes, from engineering and safety case through to infrastructure, manufacturing and operational support.
Lead multidisciplinary teams across project management, engineering, nuclear safety, human factors, digital and other specialist capabilities, bringing the right expertise together around the client's mission.
Own commercial performance, forecasting, risk, change, opportunities, financial management and project controls, maintaining delivery confidence on long-term frameworks and major commissions.
Establish effective governance, assurance and delivery arrangements that meet the expectations of nuclear, defence and other highly regulated client environments.
Guide teams through complex technical, delivery and stakeholder challenges, balancing safety, security, quality, schedule, cost and client outcomes.
Work with Portfolio, Key Account and Technical Leaders to identify emerging client needs, shape propositions, lead bids and convert strong delivery into sustainable growth.
Coach and develop project managers and wider team members, strengthening capability and encouraging knowledge sharing.
Champion project management best practice and continuous improvement across the wider business.

At Chief Project Manager level, the scope may extend to leadership of major programmes, portfolios, long-term frameworks or strategic client relationships across one or more of these core accounts.

About You

We recognise that experienced project leaders build their careers in different ways. We're interested in the strengths, perspectives and leadership experience you can bring to our core client portfolios, rather than expecting every successful candidate to have followed the same career path.

You May Bring

Significant experience leading complex engineering, infrastructure, manufacturing, energy or major project delivery, ideally within nuclear, defence or another highly regulated sector.
A strong client mindset, with experience building trusted relationships and working collaboratively with senior client, regulatory, stakeholder and delivery teams.
Confidence operating with significant accountability while creating space for others to contribute and succeed.
Strong commercial judgement, with an understanding of how delivery decisions influence client outcomes, framework performance, risk and sustainable growth.
Experience across areas such as commercial management, forecasting, risk, change, contracts, resources and financial performance.
The ability to create clarity and direction within complex or ambiguous environments.
An inclusive leadership style and a genuine interest in coaching, mentoring and developing others.
The ability to communicate complex information clearly and create alignment across multidisciplinary teams and senior stakeholders.
An ability to combine attention to detail with a strong understanding of the wider strategic and commercial picture.
Experience identifying and shaping opportunities that deepen strategic client relationships, improve delivery and expand the value we provide.

Direct experience within the civil or defence nuclear industries, or another highly regulated environment would be advantageous. We also welcome relevant leadership experience from other complex sectors.

A recognised engineering degree and/or professional project management qualification would be beneficial, but we also value experience, leadership capability and transferable strengths.

For the Chief Project Manager level, we would expect broader evidence of leadership across major projects, programmes, portfolios, long-term frameworks, strategic client relationships or business growth activities.

Above all, we're looking for people who can turn deep understanding of our clients' missions into excellent delivery: leaders who combine project and commercial judgement with inclusive leadership, trusted relationships and a genuine commitment to helping teams and clients succeed.

Rewards & benefits

Explore the rewards and benefits that help you thrive – at every stage of your life and your career. Enjoy competitive salaries, employee rewards and a brilliant range of benefits you can tailor to suit your own health, wellbeing, financial and lifestyle choices. Make the most of a myriad of opportunities for training and professional development to grow your skills and expertise. And combine our hybrid working culture and flexible holiday allowances to balance a great job and fulfilling personal life.

Rewards and benefits – Careers at AtkinsRéalis

About AtkinsRéalis

We're AtkinsRéalis, a world-class engineering services and nuclear organization. We connect people, data and technology to transform the world's'infrastructure and energy systems. Together, with our industry partners and clients, and our global team of consultants, designers, engineers and project managers, we can change the world. We're committed to leading our clients across our various end markets to engineer a better future for our planet and its people.

Find out more.

Hi, we’re SambaSafety and we offer the industry’s most comprehensive driver monitoring software. Our mission is promoting safer communities by reducing risk through data insights. Companies trust SambaSafety to keep their employees safe on the roads, price and reduce risk, help protect their brand, their bottom line, and our global community. 

We’ve built an inclusive, supportive, and exceptional culture where every employee is empowered in their role. Don’t take our word for it; we’ve been recognized as a Top Workplace by The Denver Post, Albuquerque Journal, Sacramento Bee, and Built In Colorado. And our employees rate SambaSafety as top-notch, with a rock solid Top Rating on Glassdoor.

What You’ll Do:

Job Summary:

The Technical Program Manager, Engineering owns how work moves through the SambaSafety engineering organization, from a commitment or an idea to something running in production. Reporting to the Chief Technology Officer, this role runs the cross-team programs that no single engineering pod owns: platform and data initiatives, infrastructure migrations, reliability and security remediation, and the engineering side of the company’s largest product commitments. The role keeps Jira honest, dependencies visible, risks surfaced early, and stakeholders informed, so engineering leaders decide on facts rather than status meetings.

This is a new role and the first of its kind in Engineering. It is the engineering counterpart to two neighboring functions: Product Management, which owns what gets built and why, and Global Information Systems, which delivers back-office business applications. This role owns how and when engineering work gets delivered. Where Product has a Product Manager on the work, including the data platform and entity resolution capabilities, the Technical Program Manager pairs with them: the Product Manager owns the customer and go-to-market side, and this role owns the cross-team and technical dependencies that those programs generate. Where no Product Manager is assigned, such as infrastructure migrations, security remediation, reliability, and AI tooling rollouts, the role leads the program outright, including stakeholder interviews, scoping, and story creation.

SambaSafety is adopting AI-assisted software delivery through its Concept-to-Cash framework and agentic engineering harness. The Technical Program Manager is a primary operator of that process, making sure stage gates are respected, verification is real, and tooling removes toil rather than adding process.

Role Scope:

Track: 
Individual contributor on the Engineering career path, with room to grow in scope as the program management function matures.

Reports to: 
Chief Technology Officer. No direct reports; success is measured by programs delivered and by the practices other teams adopt.

Working partners: 
Engineering Managers and Directors, Staff Engineers, Product Management, the Senior Project Manager in Global Information Systems, and external engineering partners.

Scope of programs: 
Multi-quarter initiatives touching two or more engineering teams, spanning platform and data work, engineering-only programs, and the engineering side of customer-facing product commitments.

Responsibilities:

Program ownership: 
Run several concurrent cross-pod programs end to end: charter, plan, dependencies, risks, status, and delivery.

Engineering-only programs: 
Lead outright the work no Product Manager is assigned to, such as cloud and infrastructure migrations, AI harness and tooling rollouts, security remediation, and reliability improvements.

Pairing with Product: 
Partner with the assigned Product Manager on customer-facing big rocks and on platform capabilities such as the data platform and entity resolution. Product owns scope, priority, and the customer and go-to-market side; this role owns cross-team technical dependencies, sequencing, and the delivery plan, which is where these programs most often stall today.

Discovery and scoping: 
Conduct stakeholder interviews, define scope and success measures, and record decisions so the reasoning outlives the meeting.

Jira and Confluence: 
Own the epic and story structure for programs, cross-project linking, and the Concept ID conventions that tie Confluence, Jira, and Bitbucket together. Write stories engineers can start without a second conversation, and keep program documentation in a form others can pick up and edit.

Planning cadence: 
Run the engineering side of quarterly and annual planning, track big rocks against capacity and commitments, and produce status executives can read in two minutes.

Risk and escalation: 
Surface risks early with options attached, and escalate to the right leader with a recommendation.

Delivery measurement: 
Maintain the metrics that show whether delivery is getting more predictable, including cycle time, commitment accuracy, and adoption of AI-assisted delivery practices.

Partner coordination: 
Coordinate across external engineering partners where programs depend on them, so handoffs are managed rather than discovered.

Process improvement: 
Improve how engineering plans and delivers with the lightest process that works, always explaining the why, and retire process that no longer earns its keep.

What You’ll Need:

5+ years in program, project, or product management within SaaS software organizations, including 2+ years running cross-team technical programs.

A clear track record of getting things shipped: able to point to programs delivered on commitment and the obstacles worked through to get there.

Expert in Jira and Confluence, including building epic and story structures, boards, filters, and dashboards from scratch. Familiarity with Bitbucket and CI/CD pipeline concepts.

Technical fluency: able to read an architecture diagram, understand an API contract or a data pipeline, and ask the right questions of engineers without needing to build it. AWS familiarity is a plus.

Strong stakeholder interviewing and requirements-shaping skills, with the judgment to know when a request is a real need and when it is a symptom.

Plain-spoken written and verbal communication that works for engineers and executives alike.

Comfortable using AI-assisted tools as part of daily work, and curious about how they change program management itself.

Experience with regulated data (FCRA, DPPA, or similar), data-heavy platforms, or a private-equity-backed environment is helpful but not required.

Bachelor’s degree in a technical or business field, or equivalent experience.

Benefits and Perks:

Flexible and generous Paid Time Off and Paid Volunteer Days

401k Employer Match 

Generous Healthcare Benefits 

Up to 12 weeks paid time off for maternity leave based on tenure

Wellness &Tuition Reimbursement

Flexible Work Arrangements

Lots of SambaSafety swag & SambaSafety Events 

Our team of talented and committed safety professionals is exceptional. At SambaSafety we strive to foster an inclusive culture that supports, encourages and celebrates a wide array of diversity. We are committed to create a space where all employees can show up as their authentic selves every day, and we work to advance employee equality, diversity and inclusion.

SambaSafety provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, gender identity, and expression or genetics.

Come join us to find out for yourself what all the excitement is about!

new_jobs.title: Director, Technical Program Manager (EPTech)
new_jobs.description:
Do you love driving complex technical initiatives and pioneering in the technology space? Do you enjoy solving complex business problems in a fast-paced, collaborative, inclusive, and iterative delivery environment? At Capital One, you'll be part of a big group of makers, breakers, doers and disruptors, who love to solve real problems and meet real customer needs. We are seeking Technical Program Managers who are passionate about marrying technology with business strategy to join our team. As a Technical Program Manager, you’ll have the opportunity to be on the forefront of driving major technical transformations and scaling platform capabilities across Capital One.

Enterprise Platforms Technology ( EPTech
) comprises many of Capital One’s most important enterprise platforms. We establish practices for building technology solutions across the company and deliver capabilities that exemplify those practices.

As a Director TPM in EPTech, you will leverage your technical acumen and engineering experience to drive the strategy and execution of large-scale, technically complex, cross-functional programs aligned with Capital One’s business priorities. You’ll break down complexity and organizational silos, influence roadmaps, dive deep into system design and architecture, make technical tradeoffs, drive platform consolidation, and identify, resolve, define, and escalate mitigation plans for hard technical dependencies.

What You’ll Do:

As a Director of Technical Program Management (TPM), we’re looking for someone that can help us lead programs that deliver on critical business goals and build large scale products & platforms that will help Capital One customers have incredible experiences.

In addition to the technical program, you will also work to pave the way for an expanding TPM discipline within the team, by leveraging your industry knowledge and experience to teach the organization what a great TPM can achieve.

Contribute to the organization’s TPM / Delivery strategy: establish operating mechanisms, maturity models, and tooling that scale across portfolios
Drive development of and alignment on program roadmap anchored in business objectives, definition of done, technical solutions, and sequencing of dependencies
Lead cross-platform technical investment planning and ensure architectural alignment toward long-term platform convergence and reuse
Serve as an executive-level escalation point for program risks, influencing technology leaders to make data-driven tradeoffs between speed, cost and resiliency
Ensure definition of measurable outcomes of platform success (availability, scalability, cost efficiency, developer velocity) and ensure delivery accountability across multiple engineering teams

Basic Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in a technical field
At least 7 years of experience managing technical programs

Preferred Qualifications:

7+ years of experience designing and building solutions using distributed computing or service oriented architecture (SOA)
3+ years of experience in building distributed systems & highly available services using cloud computing services / architecture - preferably using AWS
3+ years experience building highly scalable products & platforms
3+ years of experience with Agile delivery
3+ years years experience delivering large and complex programs - where you contribute to the business or technical vision, collaborate with large cross-functional teams, secure commitments on deliverables and unblock teams to land business impact
Experience in building systems & solutions within a highly regulated environment
MBA or Master’s Degree in a related technical field (Computer Science, Software Engineering)
PMP, Lean, Agile, or Six Sigma certification
3+ years of people management experience or influencing organization as an IC
Experience driving platform standardization across multiple product portfolios or lines of business
Track record of building TPM maturity (operating models, career frameworks, metrics) at scale within engineering organizations
Exceptional communication and influence skills, capable of engaging deeply with technical teams while translating implications into compelling business narratives that persuade senior leadership

The minimum and maximum full-time annual salaries for this role are listed below, by location. Please note that this salary information is solely for candidates hired to perform work within one of these locations, and refers to the amount Capital One is willing to pay at the time of this posting. Salaries for part-time roles will be prorated based upon the agreed upon number of hours to be regularly worked.

New York, NY: $251,400 - $286,900 for Director, Technical Program Management

Candidates hired to work in other locations will be subject to the pay range associated with that location, and the actual annualized salary amount offered to any candidate at the time of hire will be reflected solely in the candidate’s offer letter.

This role is also eligible to earn performance based incentive compensation, which may include cash bonus(es) and/or long term incentives (LTI). Incentives could be discretionary or non discretionary depending on the plan.

new_jobs.description:
Alternate Locations:
Radnor, PA (Pennsylvania); Charlotte, NC (North Carolina); Fort Wayne, IN (Indiana); Greensboro, NC (North Carolina)

Work Arrangement:

Hybrid : Employee will work 3 days a week in a Lincoln office

Relocation assistance:
is not available for this opportunity.

Requisition #:
76366

The Role at a Glance

As part of the AI PMO team, this position serves as the Program Manager is responsible for leading complex, cross-functional programs that deliver enterprise data platforms, data products, artificial intelligence and machine learning capabilities, and the engineering foundations required to operate them securely, reliably, and at scale.

The role translates strategic priorities and technical roadmaps into executable plans; coordinates delivery across the AI, Data and Analytics team (AIDA) ; and establishes the governance, transparency, and delivery discipline needed to manage scope, dependencies, resources, risks, and measurable outcomes from discovery through production adoption. Hands-on proficiency with Jira is essential.

What You'll Be Doing

Program Leadership

Leads the end-to-end planning, execution, and delivery of complex AI, data, and engineering programs, including data platforms, analytics products, AI/ML solutions, APIs, integrations, and cloud modernization initiatives.
Partners with engineering leaders, architects, product managers, data scientists, and business stakeholders to define program scope, priorities, success measures, and delivery approaches.
Translates product, architecture, and technology roadmaps into integrated program plans with clear milestones, dependencies, resource needs, and release targets.
Facilitates program operating rhythms, including planning sessions, dependency reviews, risk discussions, release readiness assessments, and executive updates.

Technical Program Management

Develops sufficient technical understanding to participate credibly in architecture and engineering discussions, identify risks, surface delivery gaps, and communicate tradeoffs.
Identifies, analyzes, and drives resolution of program risks, issues, and dependencies, including data quality, environment readiness, infrastructure, security, governance, and competing engineering priorities.
Coordinates delivery activities across software development, cybersecurity, architecture, privacy, data governance, AI governance, change management, and release management functions.
Drives release and production readiness across teams, including testing, deployment planning, adoption activities, support readiness, and post-implementation reviews.

Jira, Delivery Excellence & Communication

Uses Jira as the primary system of record for program execution, maintaining visibility into work, dependencies, releases, delivery progress, and program health.
Establishes delivery standards for backlog management, estimation, ownership, status reporting, dependency tracking, and release planning.
Produces clear communications and reporting for technical teams and senior leaders, including status updates, dashboards, roadmaps, risk summaries, and recommendations.
Improves program delivery practices by standardizing workflows, reporting, governance routines, and tools that increase transparency, quality, and execution speed.

What We’re Looking For

Must Haves

4 Year/Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of Bachelor's)
5 – 7+ Years experience in Project/Program Management that directly aligns with the specific responsibilities for this position
Strong understanding of software development, engineering delivery, data platforms, analytics solutions, cloud technologies, or AI/ML implementations.
Experience using Jira for planning, execution, dependency management, and reporting.
Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities and drive alignment across technical and business teams.
Strong communication, facilitation, stakeholder management, and problem-solving skills

Application Deadline

Applications for this position will be accepted through 11/30/26 subject to earlier closure due to applicant volume.

What’s it like to work here?

At Lincoln Financial, we love what we do. We make meaningful contributions each and every day to empower our customers to take charge of their lives. Working alongside dedicated and talented colleagues, we build fulfilling careers and stronger communities through a company that values our unique perspectives, insights and contributions and invests in programs that empower each of us to take charge of our own future.

What’s in it for you:

Clearly defined career tracks and job levels, along with associated behaviors for each of Lincoln's core values and leadership attributes
Leadership development and virtual training opportunities
PTO/parental leave
Competitive 401K and employee benefits
Free financial counseling, health coaching and employee assistance program
Tuition assistance program
Work arrangements that work for you
Effective productivity/technology tools and training

The pay range for this position is $106,875 - $171,000 with anticipated pay for new hires between the minimum and midpoint of the range
and could vary above and below the listed range as permitted by applicable law. Pay is based on non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, education, location, licensure requirements, proficiency and qualifications required for the role. The base pay is just one component of Lincoln’s total rewards package for employees. In addition, the role may be eligible for the Annual Incentive Program, which is discretionary and based on the performance of the company, business unit and individual. Other rewards may include long-term incentives, sales incentives and Lincoln’s standard benefits package.

About The Company

Lincoln Financial (NYSE: LNC) helps people to confidently plan for their version of a successful future. We focus on identifying a clear path to financial security, with products including annuities, life insurance, group protection, and retirement plan services.

With our 120-year track record of expertise and integrity, millions of customers trust our solutions and service to help put their goals in reach.

Lincoln Financial Distributors, a broker-dealer, is the wholesale distribution organization of Lincoln Financial. Lincoln Financial is the marketing name for Lincoln Financial Corporation and its affiliates including The Lincoln National Life Insurance Company, Fort Wayne, IN, and Lincoln Life & Annuity Company of New York, Syracuse, NY. Lincoln Financial affiliates, their distributors, and their respective employees, representatives and/or insurance agents do not provide tax, accounting or legal advice.

Lincoln is committed to creating an inclusive environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

Follow us on Facebook, X, LinkedIn, Instagram, and YouTube. For the latest company news, visit our newsroom.

If you are interested in a career at Lincoln, we encourage you to review our current openings and apply on our website. Lincoln values the privacy and security of every applicant and urges all applicants to diligently protect their sensitive personal information from scams targeting job seekers. new_jobs.title: Senior IT Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

Pueo is known for bringing the best talent and unique tools to every opportunity. Pueo's Parliament (aka workforce) is composed of professionals who are seeking the opportunity to work in a business organization that thrives on career development and independence. In support of mission and professional growth, our Parliament has supported the development of multiple patents, proprietary tools, and applications as well as trademarked processes.

Our organization emphasizes career development across multiple career environments (at the members own pace) and ensures those who contribute broadly are properly rewarded. Pueo has four career environments where every member of the parliament can participate. Each environment has opportunities available for all levels. Opportunities are framed by an employee's desires and capabilities, and we ensure challenges, growth, and unique experiences are available for employees at all levels.

Our Career Environments (Program, Functional, Service, and Leadership) provide numerous opportunities for employees to invest in their personal growth and those things that offer fulfillment. We invest in helping our members create and execute their career development plans. Our Pods (small teams of 5 or less) are comprised of personnel with similar skillsets to ensure mentorship, understanding, and peer support.

Overview

We are hiring a Senior IT Program Manager
that supports the DIA CIO RMF Program by planning, coordinating, controlling, and reporting portfolio status and Assessment and Authorization activities across an assigned portfolio. This role:

Converts Government and program priorities into executable plans
Works directly with senior Government leaders (GG-14 level and above)
Coordinates system owners, program offices, cybersecurity personnel, assessors, authorizing stakeholders, and contractor teams
Ensures schedules, risks, issues, actions, dependencies, decisions, and leadership briefings remain current and decision-ready
Owns scope, schedule, milestones, dependencies, budget tracking, and delivery governance
Maintains project plans, RAID logs, decision records, action trackers, and status reporting
Facilitates stakeholder alignment, working sessions, reviews, and executive briefings
Coordinates RMF, A&A, technical, security, program-office, customer, and contractor workstreams
Manages change control, acceptance criteria, deliverables, and project closeout
Escalates risks and decisions early with clear options, impacts, and recommendations

Skills

Strong interpersonal and communication skills to engage senior Government stakeholders
Excellent project management and organizational skills
Ability to synthesize complex information into executive-ready briefings and reports
Solid analytical and problem-solving skills for dependency and risk management
Effective facilitation and stakeholder coordination across technical and non-technical teams

Abilities

Lead or contribute to security initiatives requiring cross-functional coordination
Manage competing priorities and complex stakeholder relationships
Work effectively in classified environments
Maintain compliance with classified information protection requirements

Requirements

Mergers & Acquisitions and IT Integrations

Facilities, Office Relocations & Real Estate Projects

Lead enterprise infrastructure and technology migration projects.
Develop migration strategies, schedules, user groups, communication plans, testing requirements, cutover plans, rollback plans, and post-migration support.

Track migration progress, exceptions, remediation activities, and overall completion.

Lead projects from initiation and requirements gathering through planning, execution, implementation, stabilization, and closure.
Develop and maintain detailed project plans, schedules, milestones, dependencies, RAID logs, decision logs, and project documentation.
Manage multiple concurrent projects and workstreams across different business units and geographic regions.
Establish clear project ownership, deliverables, deadlines, and accountability across technical teams.
Facilitate project kickoffs, working sessions, status meetings, steering meetings, and post-implementation reviews.
Identify risks and issues early and drive resolution or escalation to appropriate leadership.
Ensure completed projects transition successfully into operational support.

Manage and coordinate technology initiatives associated with internal and external audits, IT controls, risk remediation, compliance, and governance requirements.

Escalate vendor risks or delivery issues that could impact project timelines or business operations.

Executive Reporting & Stakeholder Management

Provide clear and concise project reporting to the Global Head of IT Support & Operations
, IT leadership, business leadership, and other stakeholders.
Develop project dashboards covering overall status, milestones, accomplishments, upcoming activities, risks, issues, dependencies, decisions, and financial status.
Translate technical issues into understandable business impact for non-technical stakeholders.
Coordinate stakeholders across multiple teams, business units, geographic regions, and vendors.
Escalate critical risks and decisions with clearly documented impacts, options, owners, and required actions.

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, Project Management, or equivalent professional experience.
7+ years of IT project management experience

Demonstrated experience managing complex M&A integrations, infrastructure migrations, office relocations/facilities projects, and enterprise technology initiatives
.

new_jobs.title: Business Operations Manager
new_jobs.description:
Divergent is building the new industrial age. Every day, our teams design, manufacture, and assemble advanced systems for some of the world’s most demanding industries. Our integrated engineering and manufacturing platform transforms complex designs into production-ready solutions, helping customers move faster, build smarter, and deliver critical systems when they matter most. Divergent is a qualified Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and supports leading U.S. aerospace and defense companies.

Join us and help push the boundaries of what can be built.

Purpose

The Business Operations Manager is a generalist, cross-functional leader who bridges the business, data, and engineering/AI teams and is responsible for enabling high-quality, data-driven decision-making, operational alignment, and communication across the organization. This role establishes and facilitates the business processes, operating rhythms, and governance that enable Engineering, Programs, Operations, Supply Chain, Finance and other functional teams to make informed decisions, manage risk, and execute against company priorities, with a specific focus on driving efficient data flows and partnering with software/AI teams to operationalize our most critical, data-driven business decisions such as budgeting and capital investment (capex).

This role owns making the Sales, Inventory, and Operations Planning (SIOP) process more efficient and effective, facilitating aspects of it as a central cross-functional forum to align demand, supply, capacity, inventory, and financial objectives, including the inputs that feed downstream decisions like budgeting and capital planning. Beyond SIOP, this person will help identify which other operational processes the business strategically needs and then design, stand up, and lead them, bringing the same cross-functional rigor and data discipline applied to SIOP.

Success in this role requires navigating ambiguity, translating complex data into actionable insights, aligning stakeholders with competing priorities, and continually improving the systems, analytics, AI/automation tooling, and governance that support operational excellence in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.

The Role

Own aspects of and continually improve the company's monthly SIOP process, ensuring timely inputs, scenario analysis, and clear decisions at each step, while concurrently owning other strategic, cross-functional processes that affect operational decision-making and require the same rigor.
Facilitate structured business reviews, SIOP and beyond, that align Sales, Programs, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Finance and other functional teams around priorities, risks, dependencies, and execution plans.
Translate ambiguous business questions (e.g., "should we approve this capex request?") into the data, reporting structure, and process needed to answer them repeatably, not just producing a one-off analysis.
Develop and maintain trusted reporting dashboards, KPIs, and data governance processes that provide leadership with accurate, actionable insights.
Partner closely with data science, digital, and AI/automation teams to improve planning systems, reporting capabilities, automation, and analytics that support scalable business operations, including hands-on evaluation and direction of new AI-enabled tools as they become available, not just coordinating with the teams that build them.
Identify cross-functional risks, constraints, and opportunities, driving mitigation plans and ensuring decisions are documented, communicated, and executed.
Partner with Finance and functional leaders to ensure operational plans support strategic and financial objectives.
Lead continuous improvement initiatives by evaluating existing processes, identifying inefficiencies and opportunities, partnering with functional leaders to design improved ways of working, and driving measurable improvements to operational performance.
Lead implementation of process improvements through excellent project management, stakeholder coordination and buy-in, defining business requirements, supporting software system development, driving change management, and ensuring successful adoption of new processes and tools.

Basic Qualifications

Ability to lawfully access information and technology that is subject to US export controls.
Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations Management, Engineering, Business, Finance, or related field.
5 – 8+ years of progressive experience in business operations, S&OP/SIOP, program management, supply chain, production planning, engineering operations, or other cross-functional operational leadership roles within advanced manufacturing, electronics, aerospace, medical devices, or related technology-intensive sectors.
Excellent communication and facilitation skills, with a proven ability to influence and drive decisions cross-functionally and at all levels of an organization (executive leadership to execution teams).
Experience leading impactful cross-functional projects involving data and business processes.
Hands-on data query and analysis ability (e.g., SQL, Python, or R).
Able to translate an ambiguous business question into the data and reporting structure needed to answer it repeatably.
Comfortable partnering with software engineering and AI/ML teams - can scope requirements, evaluate tooling, and speak credibly about feasibility and tradeoffs without being a hands-on engineer.
Has worked in a scaling or fast-changing environment where processes had to be built from the ground up, not just inherited and maintained; comfortable with ambiguity and a lack of existing playbooks.
Track record designing and standing up new operational processes from scratch, not just optimizing existing ones.
Experience supporting recurring, high-stakes business decision cycles such as budgeting, forecasting, or capital investment (capex) approval workflows.
Preferred: platform proficiency in ERP/MRP and advanced planning or analytics tools (e.g. SAP, Oracle, Kinaxis, o9, Power BI, or similar).
Preferred: solid understanding of key supply chain concepts: forecasting, capacity planning, inventory optimization, lead-time management, and product lifecycle management.
Preferred: experience operating in a hardware technology environment, where physical production constraints (supply chain, capacity, lead times) intersect with software/data-driven decision-making.

Behavioral Competencies

Generalist mindset: equally comfortable in a finance/budgeting conversation, a process-mapping workshop, or a requirements discussion with engineers.
Growth mindset with a track record of building or maturing processes, not just operating in steady-state environments.
Comfort operating in fast-changing, ambiguous environments with imperfect data and time-constrained decisions.
Systems thinker who sees end-to-end value streams and can simplify complex data and business planning processes into high level visuals and discussions for decision-making.
Data-driven and highly analytical, comfortable challenging assumptions and using facts to resolve conflicts.
Strong collaborator who breaks down functional silos and creates shared ownership of the plan.
Bias for action, with a focus on execution, follow-through, and measurable results.
Highly organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable operating with urgency and ambiguity while still driving structure and accountability.
Strong influencer and facilitator who can navigate conflicting priorities, challenge assumptions, and align senior leaders and technical teams around difficult tradeoff decisions.

What Success Looks Like

This is a manager-level individual-contributor role. Success is measured by how much faster and more reliably the business can move from a data-driven question - budgeting, capex, or otherwise - to an operational decision, and by the quality and durability of the processes and data flows put in place to make that repeatable

Work Environment

This role is based onsite in our Torrance, CA office.

Compensation

At Divergent, our pay range is based on the level of the job. For this role, we will consider candidates at levels S06 - S07 as evaluated through our interview process.

SIOP Manager (Lead) / S06: $133,580 - $183,680

Holistic Compensation Package: Enjoy a world-class compensation package that includes a competitive salary, equity plan, and discretionary results-based incentive bonus opportunities, ensuring you're truly valued for your contributions.
Wellness and Time Off: Embrace a healthy lifestyle with paid vacation, sick time, and company holidays, including a year-end shutdown to recharge. We support growing families with paid parental leave, recognizing the importance of bonding time.
Comprehensive Health and Wellness: Prioritize your well-being with our comprehensive health and wellness benefits, offering both HMO and Premium PPO options. Additionally, benefit from company-sponsored life insurance and short and long-term disability coverage for peace of mind.
Investment in Growth: We're committed to your professional development. Take advantage of reimbursement opportunities for learning and development initiatives, empowering you to continuously expand your skill set and reach peak performance.
Collaborative and High-Performing Environment: Join our collaborative, dynamic, and high-performing team within a fast-paced, mission-driven company. Together, we're disrupting the traditional manufacturing industry, fostering innovation, and integrating people and technology to reduce our footprint.

Our advanced technology, combined with a team genuinely invested in our clients’ success, creates frictionless shopping experiences, approving more good orders, protecting revenue, and keeping customers happy.

Our people are the heart of everything we do, driving our mission forward with commitment, empathy, and creativity. Join us on our mission to empower confident, fraud-free commerce by helping online retailers provide superior customer experiences and eliminate fraud. Learn about our company values here!

Job Title:
Risk Intelligence Manager

Department: Risk Intelligence

The Risk Intelligence organization at Signifyd is responsible for proactively detecting and continuously monitoring fraud activities to mitigate immediate financial losses and protect portfolio health. This team partners closely with Data Science to improve machine learning (ML) model performance by providing continuous feedback on model outputs and identifying areas for enhancement using real-world fraud patterns and merchant feedback. We enhance detection mechanisms to reduce friction for merchants and their customers while driving revenue. We build trust through responsiveness and expertise, fostering stronger merchant relationships. We demonstrate the value of fraud prevention solutions in driving revenue growth and reducing losses.

About the role:

In this role, you will lead and develop a team of fraud analysts who investigate emerging threats, respond to fraud incidents, and translate behavioral insights into effective risk strategies. You will strengthen the people, tools, processes, and analytical standards that enable the team to succeed. This includes coaching analysts, improving investigative practices, establishing best practices, and helping team members develop the skills needed to solve increasingly complex risk problems.

You will partner closely with Risk leadership and teams across Data Science, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering. Together, you will turn investigative findings into scalable improvements that reduce fraud losses, support intelligent risk-taking, and improve customer experiences. Success in this role requires strong people leadership, analytical judgment, operational discipline, and the ability to communicate complex risk issues clearly to technical, business, and customer audiences.

At Signifyd, you will be part of a purpose-driven company dedicated to creating a dynamic and versatile work environment. Risk Intelligence is an integral part of our growing organization that values neighborly collaboration, passion, and inventiveness.

Responsibilities:

Hire, coach, and performance-manage a team of fraud analysts, closing skill gaps and serving as the escalation resource for complex investigations and emerging attacks.
Own and improve the standards, playbooks, and tools for incident response, case review, merchant onboarding, decision transparency, and rule design where historical data is limited.
Turn investigative findings into clear recommendations for the teams responsible for business and customer outcomes, and represent Risk Intelligence in cross-functional initiatives.
Partner with business-unit leaders, Data Science, Customer Success, Product, and Engineering to close capability gaps and turn fraud behaviors into durable signals, features, and model improvements.
Support customer conversations as a fraud subject-matter expert, explaining risk decisions and sharing effective practices. Coach analysts to communicate risk insights clearly and build confidence presenting to customers.

Requirements:

3+ years of direct people management, including coaching and performance management, with a track record of building an effective team.
5+ years in ecommerce, payments, fraud prevention, or risk management, including fraud investigations and emerging-threat response.
Advanced analytical judgment, including balancing fraud losses, customer experience, and intelligent risk-taking.
Experience building operational standards, playbooks, and workflows, and the discipline to improve how a team works.
Effective communication skills presenting to a variety of technical, business, and customer audiences
Solid cross-functional experience partnering with data science, customer success, product, or engineering.

new_jobs.title: Market Intelligence Analyst
new_jobs.description:
About Us

What if your work could drive change in a globally established industry, shaping processes that touch every corner of the world? At Forto, we are at the forefront of change, harnessing the power of AI to revolutionise logistics. We want to reinvent digital supply chains to be transparent, frictionless and sustainable. From day one, our mission has been to simplify global trade – creating a seamless and efficient logistics process.

Position Summary

The Market Intelligence Analyst serves as the central intelligence capability covering four key pillars: macro and trade lane, carrier, competitor, and customer/segment intelligence. Covering ocean, air, and rail freight across major global lanes, this role translates complex market data into actionable commercial insights. Crucially, the analyst is responsible for providing credible, data-backed intelligence that directly influences both short-term pricing actions and long-term pricing strategy. A primary measure of success in this role is the ability to spot commercial signals from external sources ahead of time and coherently alert leadership to impending market shifts before they fully materialize.

Key Responsibilities

Commercial Signaling & Pricing Influence

Provide credible, quantitative market intelligence to directly influence short-term pricing decisions and shape the long-term pricing outlook.
Proactively monitor external sources and macroeconomic indicators to spot early commercial signals and leading indicators of structural market shifts.
Coherently present forward-looking pricing outlooks, flagging external market changes ahead of time to allow commercial teams to adjust strategy proactively.
Evolve the macro data dashboard into a predictive internal demand signal that the Trade team directly prices against, rather than acting as a retrospective report.

Recurring Deliverables & Market Reporting

Author and publish fixed-cadence outputs, including a Monthly Export Newsletter for external shippers and internal Sales, and a Weekly Intel Digest.
Produce the comprehensive Quarterly Market Update (Internal & External Webinar versions), encompassing economic outlooks and sea freight analysis.
Maintain and refresh the internal MI Data Dashboard monthly, aggregating macro indicators (GDP, PMI, inflation, retail sales) across 9 core geographies.
Execute weekly manual updates of rate and index pulls to maintain continuous historical data series.

Strategic Analysis & Geopolitical Scenarios

Maintain live forward-looking frameworks, including trigger forward calendars and comprehensive trigger playbooks.
Conduct deep-dive market-entry and lane assessments evaluating dimensions like consolidation, agency restarts, and FTA campaigns.

Cross-Functional Enablement & Crisis Management

Provide continuous operational and enablement support for Marketing, Sales, Operations, Legal, and Finance.
Manage ad-hoc crisis communications, such as the Middle East crisis page updates, bilingual notice templates, and customer FAQs regarding major disruptions.

Required Skills And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Economics, Business, Supply Chain or a related analytical field, or equivalent practical experience.
2+ years in market intelligence, market research, or business or commercial analysis, ideally in a B2B environment.
Strong B2B commercial sense: you understand supplier and customer dynamics and can see how market events affect rates, volumes and customer relationships.
Experience gathering and checking information from many sources (websites, industry reports, news, financial results) and turning it into clear, accurate insight.
Confident everyday use of AI tools (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini) to work faster, with the discipline to fact-check and add your own judgement.
Solid Excel / Google Sheets skills and comfort with numbers, trends and indices.
Clear, concise communication in English, with the ability to explain complex developments simply to internal teams and customers.
A curious, proactive mindset. You notice the small signals others miss and explain what they mean for the business.

Preferred Skills And Experience

Experience in freight forwarding, container shipping or wider logistics.
Familiarity with freight market data sources (e.g. SCFI, Drewry WCI, Freightos FBX, Xeneta, Sea-Intelligence).
A background in academic or market research, or in another complex B2B industry.
Experience writing customer-facing communications or market updates.
SQL, Python or dashboarding skills are a plus.

Don’t fit all of our criteria? That’s okay! We know that you might be hesitant to apply if you don’t meet all our requirements, but here at Forto, we pride ourselves on embracing diverse perspectives and celebrating potential. If you are passionate about this position and the Forto values, please apply anyway. There could be a place for you in this role – or another one that’s a perfect fit!

Why work with us?

Our team is hard-working, constantly seeking to maximise the impact of their work, but we put our people first, always winning with care. We value efficient systems and swift, direct communication. We want everyone to have their time to speak, so that we can embrace diverse perspectives to help drive towards solutions always.

Senior Data Analyst

Who We Are

Teranet is Canada’s leader in the delivery and transformation of statutory registry services with extensive expertise in land and commercial registries. We also market insightful property and data solutions, as well as practice management automation to thousands of customers in the real estate, financial services, government, utilities, and legal markets. Connect. Grow. Thrive Together.

To learn more about who we are, visit our website: www.teranet.ca

About the Role

We are seeking a Senior Data Analyst to join our Commercial Solutions Product Management team, where data and analytics play a key role in shaping product strategy and client solutions. While part of Product Management, this is a hands-on data and analytics role focused on delivering high-quality analysis and data-driven solutions.

This role combines data analysis, business & product analysis, and client-focused solution delivery. You will work across Product, Sales, Technology, and clients to understand problems, shape the right approach, and deliver actionable outputs. You will operate as a thought partner, helping define problems, clarify requirements, and translate them into effective data solutions, while owning delivery end-to-end.

A critical part of this role is protecting and strengthening our core data offerings. This includes ownership of recurring and ad hoc data deliverables, ensuring consistent quality, reliability, and continuous improvement. You will also contribute to revenue growth by supporting custom data solutions, enabling product initiatives, and providing analytical input into new data-driven offerings.

What You’ll Be Doing

This role focuses on analysis, data delivery, mentorship, and stakeholder collaboration across both ongoing operations and new initiatives. You will…
Analyze data to generate insights that support product, client, and business decisions
Translate business needs into analytical approaches (requirements, use cases, impacts)
Design and deliver data solutions (queries, datasets, reports - recurring and ad hoc)
Own outputs end-to-end, ensuring accuracy, quality, and usability
Maintain and improve recurring data deliverables, protecting core revenue streams
Partner with Product and Sales on custom data solutions, business cases, and new offerings
Support research and analysis that informs product strategy and market insights
Collaborate across Product, Sales, Technology, and clients to align on priorities and outcomes
Communicate insights clearly through presentations, dashboards, and reports
Improve and optimize workflows using modern tools, automation, and AI-assisted approaches
Provide ongoing guidance, mentorship, and quality oversight to junior team members, helping elevate team output and consistency

About You

You are an experienced analyst who brings together strong technical skills, sound business judgment, and clear communication.

Technical Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in quantitative fields (E.g., Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Engineering)
5+ years of experience in data, analytics, or business/data roles
Experience working with both business and technical stakeholders
Strong proficiency in SQL, Python, and Excel is required.
Experience with visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI)
Experience working with large datasets and data modelling
Familiarity with modern data platforms and tools
Experience using automation or AI-assisted tools to improve workflows, efficiency, and output quality
Understanding of real estate and mortgage lending data, land registration concepts, and property-related datasets is considered an asset.
Knowledge of GIS concepts and experience using spatial analysis tools such as ArcGIS is considered an asset.

Core Capabilities:

Strong analytical thinking across data, business, and product problems
Ability to break down problems, gather requirements, and assess impacts
Hands-on experience delivering end-to-end data solutions
Clear communication of insights and recommendations
Ability to manage priorities and deliver high-quality work independently
Strong problem-solving and critical thinking, with a solution-oriented mindset
Demonstrates ownership, accountability, and initiative in driving outcomes
A natural inclination to mentor and support others, taking responsibility for team quality and development without needing direction
Curiosity and willingness to explore and adopt new tools and approaches, including AI-assisted capabilities.

What Success Looks Like

You bring clarity and structure to complex problems
You ask the right questions and help refine requirements
You deliver high-quality, reliable outputs
that are clear, accurate, and ready for use
You maintain momentum and alignment across stakeholders
You translate data into clear, actionable insights
You build trust with both internal teams and clients
You take ownership of recurring and ad hoc data deliverables, ensuring consistency and continuous improvement

You actively support and mentor junior team members,
helping raise the quality and consistency of team outputs
You are proactive and self-directed, taking initiative to move work forward without needing close guidance or constant follow-up
You are comfortable taking ownership of problems and moving them forward, even when there isn’t a clearly defined path and the work involves ambiguity

Let’s Talk Pay

We believe in being upfront about pay and helping you make informed decisions about your career. The annual pay range for this role is $106,040 - $114,400 CAD
, inclusive of base salary and target incentive pay. We understand that great talent comes in many forms, each with unique skills, experience, and potential. Your salary will be tailored to reflect the experience you bring and the impact you’re ready to have on this role.

100% Employer Paid Health Benefit Plan

Paid Vacation, Floater Days & Sick Leaves
Maternity, Parental and/or Adoption Leave Top-Up Programs

Employee Assistance Program – for you and your loved ones!

At Teranet, we use smart technology to make hiring faster and more efficient. Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools help us review applications and identify strong matches—but the real decisions? Those are made by our awesome people.

Every interaction you’ll have, and every decision we make, is led by humans. AI may support us, but it’s human connection that drives every hire.

Our Career Environments (Program, Functional, Service, and Leadership) provide numerous opportunities for employees to invest in their personal growth and those things that offer fulfillment. We invest in helping our members create and execute their career development plans. Our Pods (small teams of 5 or less) are comprised of personnel with similar skillsets to ensure mentorship, understanding, and peer support.

Overview

The Zero Trust Data Analyst supports the CIO Zero Trust program by collecting, validating, analyzing, and reporting data that informs program decisions, maturity assessments, performance tracking, risk identification, and implementation planning. This mid-level role works with program, technical, architecture, finance, and mission stakeholders to turn fragmented program data, technical inputs, metrics, and reporting requirements into accurate, decision-ready products.

The Data Analyst develops and maintains dashboards, trackers, data models, briefings, and recurring reports that provide visibility into Zero Trust initiatives, capability progress, dependencies, gaps, funding, risks, and outcomes. The role supports data calls, governance reviews, leadership updates, and audit or compliance responses, while ensuring data is traceable, appropriately sourced, consistently defined, and protected in accordance with security requirements.

General Duties

Collect, clean, validate, reconcile, and maintain program data from authoritative sources, including project trackers, architecture artifacts, requirements, risk registers, data calls, meeting records, implementation plans, and stakeholder inputs.
Develop repeatable data collection methods, templates, data dictionaries, naming conventions, metric definitions, quality checks, and reporting procedures for Zero Trust program data.
Analyze Zero Trust implementation data to identify trends, gaps, dependencies, blockers, risks, ownership issues, schedule impacts, and opportunities for improved execution.
Build and maintain dashboards, scorecards, charts, briefing visuals, status reports, and executive-ready summaries that communicate program performance, maturity, and risk posture.
Support Zero Trust maturity assessments, capability mapping, pillar reporting, milestone tracking, and leadership decision support using quantitative and qualitative data.
Coordinate with technical teams, pillar advisors, architects, program managers, governance staff, cybersecurity personnel, and mission stakeholders to gather, clarify, and validate data inputs.
Maintain traceability between reported metrics, source data, assumptions, calculations, responsible owners, reporting periods, and supporting documentation.
Respond to data calls and support recurring reporting requirements by preparing accurate, timely, and well-documented responses for program leadership and Government stakeholders.
Perform quality reviews to identify inconsistent, incomplete, outdated, duplicate, or conflicting data and coordinate with data owners to resolve discrepancies.
Recommend improvements to data management, reporting workflows, automation, dashboards, and analytic products to reduce manual effort and improve leadership visibility.

Required Qualifications

Working knowledge of data analysis methods, data quality management, metric development, dashboarding, reporting, and data visualization practices.
Knowledge of program metrics, maturity tracking, risk reporting, and federal or DoD program reporting environments.
Familiarity with data sources and artifacts such as project trackers, risk registers, requirements, architecture inventories, implementation schedules, data calls, and governance records.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, data validation, and data reconciliation skills.
Proficiency with Tableau, Python, SQL, as well as Microsoft Excel, SharePoint, Teams, PowerPoint, and common collaboration or task-tracking tools.
Ability to develop data dictionaries, metric definitions, dashboards, trackers, scorecards, charts, and executive-ready analytic products.
Strong technical writing and briefing skills, including the ability to summarize complex data, assumptions, trends, gaps, and risks for technical and non-technical audiences.
Ability to turn incomplete, inconsistent, or fragmented information into reliable analytic outputs and decision-support products.
Ability to manage multiple reporting cycles, data calls, dashboards, and stakeholder requests under tight deadlines.
Ability to work across technical, program, cybersecurity, architecture, acquisition, finance, and mission teams while protecting sensitive information.
Ability to identify data issues, clarify assumptions, document limitations, and elevate risks or inconsistencies appropriately.

Education And Experience

Bachelor’s degree in Data Analytics, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Analytics, or a related discipline.
Minimum of 12 years of work experience required. Work experience must include a minimum of 4 years performing data analysis, reporting, dashboard development, metrics tracking, business intelligence, or program analysis.
Demonstrated experience collecting, cleaning, validating, reconciling, analyzing, and presenting data from multiple sources in support of leadership reporting or operational decision-making.
Experience developing dashboards, trackers, charts, scorecards, briefing visuals, data dictionaries, metric definitions, or recurring status reports using Tableau, Excel, SharePoint, or similar tools.
Experience supporting federal, DoD, IC, cybersecurity, enterprise IT, Zero Trust, or large-scale modernization programs preferred.

Certifications

Preferred but not required: Tableau Desktop Specialist, Tableau Certified Data Analyst, Tableau Certified Consultant, Microsoft Excel Expert, Certified Analytics Professional, data analytics, or visualization-related credentials.

Clearance

Active Top Secret clearance minimum required

Notre jeunesse nous rend aussi conquérants. A raison ! Notre Groupe Banque/Assurance accompagne plus de 20 millions de clients, ce qui fait de nous le 3ème groupe du secteur en France.

Environnement de travail :
La Direction de la Conformité du Groupe LBP (DCG) a pour missions d'organiser et de piloter la Conformité de LBP SA et de ses filiales, ce qui inclut :-Les règles de conduite et de lutte anti-corruption ;-Les règles des services bancaires notamment la protection de la clientèle ;-Les services d'investissement ;-Les règles en matière de Sécurité Financière, de lutte contre la Fraude et la LCB-FT.La Direction de la Sécurité Financière (DSF) met en œuvre les dispositions réglementaires en matière de Sécurité Financière (LCB-FT, Sanctions - Embargos et KYC).Elle définit les standards du Groupe LBP applicables en matière de Sécurité Financière et s'assure de la conformité et de l'adéquation des dispositifs mis en œuvre dans ce cadre sur l'ensemble des entités du groupe LBP. Par ailleurs, elle a en charge les relations avec la direction LCB-FT de l'ACPR, Tracfin et la DG Trésor.Le département « Appui opérationnel, Scénarios et Pilotages » dont les activités sont transverses au sein de la DSF, vise à soutenir le programme de celle-ci, conformément aux orientations du Directoire et de la Direction Conformité du Groupe LBP, à savoir :-la mise en place et le suivi du déploiement des solutions visant à assurer une efficacité opérationnelle, dans un contexte de croissance soutenue du volume d'activité des différents départements ;-l'animation et la coordination, entre la Direction de la Transformation et les départements métiers de la DSF, du déploiement de la couverture des risques notamment via l'IA, afin de positionner la Banque aux meilleurs pratiques du marché ;-le pilotage et le suivi des risques BC-FT / Sanctions financières & Embargos pour le périmètre du sous-groupe LBP, notamment dans le cadre des recommandations disciplinaires ou de contrôle interne afin de renforcer la solidité du dispositif de Sécurité Financière.L'ensemble de ces axes s'inscrit dans un contexte de renforcement du cadre réglementaire LCB-FT-SF, d'une coopération accrue avec les autorités compétentes de LCB-FT, de la prise en compte des attentes en matière de gouvernance du risque BC-FT notamment en lien avec le pôle assurantiel du groupe, et enfin d'une nécessaire évolution du modèle de surveillance des opérations.

Accompagnement à la prise de poste
:
Un accompagnement managérial et RH sera envisagé en fonction de vos compétences précédemment acquises et de votre expérience. Selon votre parcours professionnel, un programme d'intégration vous sera également proposé.

Maintenant qu’on se connait, on vous en dit plus sur le poste ?

Rattaché(e) au Responsable du département AOSP, vous serez en charge des questions relatives à la donnée au sein du département. A ce titre, vous devrez notamment :

Accompagner la montée en expertise du département et plus largement de la direction sur l’utilisation des données à sa disposition
Assister, voire représenter, le Responsable du département, dans les instances relatives à la question des données
Améliorer l’exploitation actuelle faite des données disponibles au sein du département notamment dans une logique d’efficience
Accompagner les projets de mise à disposition de nouvelles données
Réaliser des analyses métier de premier de niveau à partir des données disponibles.

Au-delà de ces missions principales, vous serez sollicité(e) ponctuellement sur les autres volets du département.

Votre formation, vos expériences ?

Dans l'idéal, vous êtes titulaire d’un diplôme de niveau BAC+5, vous disposez d’une expérience professionnelle de 3 à 5 ans dans un environnement similaire. Vous maîtrisez les compétences clés suivantes :

Connaissance réglementaire et opérationnelle de base en matière LCB-FT / Sanctions financières et des enjeux associés
Maitrise des techniques d’exploitation, d’analyse et de visualisation des données hétérogènes
Maitrise des outils et technologies d’exploitation de la donnée : Python (notamment les librairies Pandas et Pyspark), Dataiku, Hive, SQL…
Connaissance en matière de gestion de projet relatif à la donnée
Connaissance de l’environnement bancaire et financier
Esprit d’analyse et capacité de synthèse, qualités rédactionnelles
Pragmatisme et approche « utilisateur »

Quels seront votre salaire et avantages ?

Cette rémunération est composée d’un salaire fixe versé sur 12 mois, d’une rémunération variable, dont le montant pourra varier selon l’atteinte d’objectifs individuels et collectifs, de l’intéressement et de la participation.

Ce package est complété par différents avantages : une couverture santé prévoyance, sans cotisation supplémentaire pour vos enfants à charge, un plan d’épargne entreprise et retraite, une prise en charge des frais de repas (tickets restaurants ou accès au restaurant d’entreprise) et les offres du Comité Social et Économique (CSE), selon l'ancienneté. Vous pourrez bénéficier de la politique de télétravail et vous aurez également accès à nos différentes formations et à nos multiples possibilités d’évolution au sein du Groupe.

Envie de postuler ? Déposez votre candidature dans votre espace.

Pour voir si on est fait pour s’entendre, on vous proposera un entretien opérationnel et un entretien RH pour exprimer vos motivations puis vous réaliserez un test de personnalité afin de déterminer vos soft skills. Et si on décide de travailler ensemble, vous suivrez un processus d’intégration digitalisé et personnalisé.

Banque citoyenne, La Banque Postale s’engage en faveur de la diversité et de l’égalité des chances pour donner accès à tous ses métiers sans discrimination de genre, d’origine sociale ou culturelle, d’orientation sexuelle ou de handicap.

Description

Amazon's Worldwide Grocery Stores, Growth & Development team is seeking a Sr. Construction Program Manager, a leader who combines deep construction industry expertise with the strategic vision and operational rigor needed to build scalable programs from the ground up. This is a program-focused role, not a Construction Project Manager position. You'll design governance frameworks, formalize what doesn't exist, fix what's broken at a systemic level, and equip hundreds of team members to do their jobs more effectively through disciplined Procore adoption, structured training, and scalable SOPs.

As our portfolio scales, information must flow end-to-end with minimal manual intervention, and every team member from Design to Construction Project Managers to Store Operations must be appropriately equipped to operate within governed, consistent processes. You will own that outcome - not by managing individual projects, but by designing, governing, and continuously improving the systems, standards, and tools that construction teams operate within so that our team can successfully execute individual project outcomes.

Key job responsibilities

Responsibilities

This role spans construction program strategy, platform governance, and organizational enablement across a portfolio of more than 600 active pipeline projects and growing. Core responsibilities include:

Develop and govern company policy, construction standards, and the Whole Foods Market (WFM) standard construction specification book.
Own end-to-end Procore process governance for execution teams (RFI, Submittals, Bidding Tool, and PCO/CCO workflows) and ensure information flows seamlessly across the construction lifecycle.
Advocate for system enhancements, integrations, and functionality improvements that drive scalability as the portfolio grows.
Govern value engineering review processes and cost governance frameworks across the construction portfolio.
Partner with Strategic Category Management and Vendor Management on GC performance assessment and scorecard frameworks.
Develop and govern permitting and entitlements coordination frameworks across multiple jurisdictions.
Define milestone frameworks and scheduling standards that Construction Operations Groups operate within.
Build and deliver role-based training curricula, SOP libraries, and change management programs for Procore and Coupa adoption.
Identify AI and automation opportunities within construction workflows and develop roadmaps in partnership with the LSA Product Management team.

A day in the life

No two days look exactly the same. You start your morning reviewing Procore compliance dashboards, flagging a pattern in stalled submittals (a process gap, not a project problem) for leadership. Mid-morning, you're presenting a business case for a Bidding Tool integration to a Procore Steering Committee. After lunch, you're facilitating cross-functional alignment across Pipeline, Indirect Procurement, and Construction teams. Late afternoon, you're delivering a Procore onboarding session using a curriculum you built. By end of week, you've advanced two SOPs, submitted enhancement requests, and documented a training gap to close next quarter.

About The Team

Amazon's Worldwide Retail Grocery Development (WWRGD) team manages the full lifecycle of Amazon and Whole Foods Market grocery retail and industrial facilities — from pre-lease due diligence through construction delivery, facilities maintenance, and decommissioning. With more than 600 active sites, 100+ active pipeline locations, and a portfolio scaling toward 2,000+ active projects, we operate at the intersection of construction, technology, and organizational scale. Our mission is to deliver best-in-class facilities faster, at best value, and with greater consistency across every site we build and maintain.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor's degree
7+ years of project management, real estate development, architecture/design experience
Experience in construction, or experience developing MOPs and SWMS for planned works
Demonstrated Procore expertise across RFI, Submittals, Bidding, Change Management, and PCO/CCO financial workflow modules
Experience developing and governing permitting, entitlements, and regulatory compliance frameworks across multiple jurisdictions
Proficiency in data analysis and reporting with ability to translate construction program data into executive-facing insights (PowerBI or equivalent)

Preferred Qualifications

Experience developing and implementing training programs
Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, or experience in project, program or product management with focus on technical education programs
Experience using managed ML/AI solutions
Experience in grocery retail, food service, or temperature-controlled facility construction environments
